questions.questionEn: After a dramatic rescue call, you notice your partner has posted a photo on Instagram showing the crash scene, including the patient's distinctive tattooed arm visible on the stretcher. The caption reads "Another wild night." What is the best action?
questions.questionZh: 一次惊险的救援任务结束后，你发现搭档在 Instagram 上发了一张事故现场照片，担架上患者带有独特纹身的手臂清晰可见，配文是"又是疯狂的一夜"。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Say nothing for now, because the patient's face is not shown and the account is set to private
options.zh: 先不说什么——照片没露脸，账号也设成了仅好友可见的私密模式

options.en: Ask your partner to delete the post now, since the tattoo identifies the patient, and report the breach
options.zh: 请搭档立刻删帖（纹身足以认出患者），并按机构规定上报这次隐私泄露

options.en: Comment on the post asking your partner to blur the tattoo, so the photo can stay up safely
options.zh: 在帖子下留言，请搭档把纹身打码，这样照片就可以安全地保留

options.en: Wait until the shift ends and raise it casually over coffee, so you avoid tension while still on the truck
options.zh: 等下班后喝咖啡时再随口提一句，免得当班的时候在车上和搭档闹得不愉快

questions.explanationEn: A distinctive tattoo can identify a patient without a face, so this is a confidentiality breach whatever the privacy setting. The professional response is immediate: get the post removed and report the breach through your service's process, because the breach has already happened even if the post comes down. A is wrong because a private account still shows the image to followers, some of whom may know the patient. C is wrong because a public comment draws more attention to the post and leaves the image online. D is wrong because every hour of delay keeps identifiable patient information circulating.
questions.explanationZh: 独特的纹身即使不露脸也能让人认出患者，所以无论账号是否私密，这都已经违反了保密义务。专业的做法是立即处理：让帖子删除，并按机构流程上报——即使帖子删了，泄露也已经发生。A 错：私密账号照样把照片展示给关注者，其中可能就有认识患者的人。C 错：公开留言只会让更多人注意到这条帖子，照片也仍挂在网上。D 错：每拖一个小时，可识别的患者信息就多传播一个小时。

questions.questionEn: After you help an elderly man up from a fall with no injuries, he presses a $50 bill into your hand and says, “Buy yourselves coffee, you deserve it.” What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你帮一位跌倒但没有受伤的老人站起来后，他往你手里塞了一张 50 加元的钞票，说：“拿去买杯咖啡吧，你们应得的。”你应该怎么做？

options.en: Accept it so he is not embarrassed, then quietly donate the money to a charity after the shift
options.zh: 先收下免得他难堪，下班后再悄悄把钱捐给慈善机构

options.en: Accept it only if your partner witnesses the exchange and you record the gift in your report
options.zh: 只要搭档在场见证、并在报告里记下这笔赠予，就可以收下

options.en: Refuse firmly and document the offer as an attempted bribe, so there is a record if asked later
options.zh: 严词拒绝，并把这次赠予记录为企图行贿，以备日后有人追问时有据可查

options.en: Thank him warmly but decline, explain crews cannot accept money, and say he can thank the service
options.zh: 真诚道谢但婉拒，说明救护人员不能收钱，并告诉他可以向机构表达感谢

questions.explanationEn: Taking money from patients compromises professional integrity and can exploit the gratitude of vulnerable people, so it must be declined — kindly, so the relationship is preserved. Pointing him to the service's feedback route respects his wish to say thanks. A is wrong because donating it later does not change the fact that you accepted cash from a patient while on duty. B is wrong because a witness and a note only document the problem; they do not make accepting money acceptable. C is wrong because a grateful man's thank-you is not a bribe, and treating it as one is disproportionate and humiliating.
questions.explanationZh: 收取患者的钱有损职业操守，也可能利用了弱势人群的感激之情，所以必须拒绝——但要客气，不伤害彼此的关系。告诉他可以向机构反馈表扬，也照顾到了他想表达感谢的心意。A 错：事后捐掉并不能改变你当班时收了患者现金这一事实。B 错：有人见证、写进记录，只是把问题记录下来，并不会让收钱变得合理。C 错：一位老人出于感激的心意不是行贿，当成行贿处理既反应过度，也让对方难堪。

questions.questionEn: Your brother-in-law owns a private non-emergency transfer company. On a call, a stable patient who does not need an ambulance asks how she can get to a specialist appointment across town tomorrow. What is the most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 你的姐夫开了一家私营非紧急转运公司。一次出勤中，一位病情稳定、不需要救护车的患者问你，她明天怎样才能去城另一头看专科门诊。最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: Recommend your brother-in-law's company, but tell her openly about the family connection first
options.zh: 推荐姐夫的公司，但先坦白告诉她你们之间的亲属关系

options.en: Give her neutral information on the available options and let her choose, promoting no company
options.zh: 中立地介绍各种出行方式，让她自己选，不推销任何公司

options.en: Recommend his company without mentioning the connection, since you know its service is good
options.zh: 推荐他的公司但不提亲属关系，反正你知道这家公司服务确实好

options.en: Decline to discuss transport at all, since any advice from you could look like a conflict
options.zh: 完全不谈出行问题，因为你给出的任何建议都可能被看成利益冲突

questions.explanationEn: A conflict of interest exists when a personal or financial interest could influence the advice you give a patient. Giving neutral information meets her need while keeping your family's business out of your professional advice. A is wrong because disclosure alone does not remove the conflict: a patient who relies on you may feel pressured to accept, and steering business to your family from a patient encounter is still inappropriate. C is wrong because hiding the relationship makes the conflict deceptive, however good the company is. D is wrong because refusing to help at all abandons a reasonable patient need; managing a conflict means removing your interest from the advice, not withholding help.
questions.explanationZh: 当个人或经济利益可能影响你给患者的建议时，就存在利益冲突。中立地介绍各种选择，既满足了患者的需要，又把自家生意排除在专业建议之外。A 错：坦白关系并不能消除冲突——依赖你的患者可能不好意思拒绝，而借出勤机会为亲属招揽生意本身就不恰当。C 错：隐瞒关系会让利益冲突变成欺瞒，公司再好也一样。D 错：干脆什么都不说等于对患者的合理需要置之不理；处理利益冲突是把个人利益从建议中剔除，而不是拒绝提供帮助。

questions.questionEn: At the grocery store, your neighbour says: "I saw your ambulance at the Chen house last night — is old Mr. Chen okay? We're all worried." What is the appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 在超市里，邻居对你说："昨晚我看到你们的救护车停在陈家门口——陈老先生还好吗？我们都很担心。"恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: Give only general reassurance, such as “he's in good hands,” since the neighbour is worried
options.zh: 既然邻居是真心担心，就只给一句笼统的安慰，比如“他已经得到妥善照顾了”

options.en: Confirm that your crew attended the call, but decline to share any of his medical details
options.zh: 确认你们出了那趟任务，但不透露他的任何病情细节

options.en: Explain kindly that you can't confirm or discuss any call, and suggest they ask the family
options.zh: 友善地解释你不能确认或讨论任何出勤情况，建议他们直接问候陈家家人

options.en: Suggest the neighbour phone the hospital for an update, since staff there can tell him more
options.zh: 建议邻居打电话到医院问问最新情况，那边的工作人员能告诉他更多

questions.explanationEn: Confidentiality covers not only clinical details but the very fact that a call happened and who it involved; information goes only to people with a need to know. Redirecting the neighbour to the family respects their concern without disclosing anything. A is wrong because “he's in good hands” confirms there was a call and that Mr. Chen is a patient. B is wrong because confirming that you attended is itself a disclosure of protected information. D is wrong because pointing the neighbour to the hospital implies Mr. Chen was taken there, which is also a disclosure.
questions.explanationZh: 保密义务不仅涵盖病情细节，也包括“是否出过这趟任务、涉及谁”这一事实本身；信息只能告诉确有必要知道的人。把邻居引向陈家家人，既尊重了他们的关心，又没有透露任何信息。A 错：“他已经得到妥善照顾了”等于确认出过任务、陈先生是患者。B 错：确认出勤本身就是在透露受保护的信息。D 错：让邻居去问医院，暗示了陈先生被送到了医院，这同样是一种泄露。

questions.questionEn: Restocking after a call, you realize you gave the patient double the intended dose of a medication. The patient is already at the hospital and appeared stable at handover. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 任务结束补充物资时，你发现刚才给患者用的药量是预定剂量的两倍。患者已经在医院，交接时看起来情况稳定。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Note it privately as a learning point since the patient was stable and no harm is apparent
options.zh: 既然患者稳定、也看不出伤害，就私下记为一次教训

options.en: Quietly amend the record so the documented dose matches what was intended
options.zh: 悄悄修改记录，让文档上的剂量与预定剂量一致

options.en: Notify the receiving hospital staff and your supervisor right away, and complete a patient safety incident report
options.zh: 立即通知接收医院的工作人员和你的主管，并填写患者安全不良事件报告

options.en: Monitor whether the hospital reports any problem before deciding whether to tell anyone
options.zh: 先观察医院是否报告异常，再决定要不要告诉别人

questions.explanationEn: Commitment to patient safety means immediate, honest reporting: the hospital must know the actual dose to monitor for effects, and the incident report allows the system to learn and prevent recurrence. Waiting or staying silent leaves the patient exposed to unmonitored risk, and altering the record to hide an error is falsification — a far more serious professional breach than the error itself.
questions.explanationZh: 对患者安全的承诺意味着立即、诚实地报告：医院必须知道实际用药剂量才能监测反应，而不良事件报告能让系统吸取教训、防止再次发生。等待或沉默会让患者暴露在无人监测的风险中，而篡改记录掩盖错误属于伪造文书——比用药错误本身严重得多的职业过失。

questions.questionEn: During a vehicle check you see your partner — a close friend going through a difficult divorce — slip a vial of medication from the drug kit into their pocket. When you ask, they say "It's nothing, don't worry about it" and change the subject. What must you do?
questions.questionZh: 车辆检查时，你看到搭档——一位正在经历艰难离婚的好友——把药品箱里的一支药悄悄放进了口袋。你问起时，对方说"没什么，别管了"就岔开了话题。你必须怎么做？

options.en: Report what you observed to a supervisor promptly, even though your partner is a close friend
options.zh: 尽快向主管报告你所看到的情况，即使搭档是你的好友

options.en: Watch them closely for the rest of the block and report only if it happens again
options.zh: 在接下来的班次里密切观察，只有再次发生才上报

options.en: Insist they return the vial, and consider the matter closed if they do
options.zh: 坚持让对方把药放回去，只要照做就当此事了结

options.en: Leave an anonymous note in their locker urging them to self-report and get help before it happens again
options.zh: 在对方储物柜里留一张匿名纸条，劝其在再次发生之前自行上报并寻求帮助

questions.explanationEn: Medication diversion endangers patients, the public, and the colleague themselves, and paramedics have an explicit duty to report unprofessional or unethical behaviour when observed. Friendship and sympathy for their circumstances do not change the obligation. Monitoring, private resolution, or anonymous notes all leave a potentially impaired provider caring for patients and an unexplained gap in controlled medications — reporting also opens the door to getting your friend real help.
questions.explanationZh: 私自挪用药品会危及患者、公众以及这位同事本人，而救护人员有明确义务在目睹不专业或不道德行为时上报。友情和对其处境的同情不能改变这一义务。观察、私下解决或匿名纸条都会让一个可能状态受损的救护人员继续照护患者，也让受管制药品的缺口无从解释——上报同时也是让你的朋友获得真正帮助的开始。

questions.questionEn: A quality review flags a call from last month where you did not apply spinal motion restriction to a patient who met the criteria. Your supervisor asks you to discuss the call. What is the professional response?
questions.questionZh: 质量审查指出你上个月的一趟任务中，未给一名符合指征的患者实施脊柱活动限制。主管请你来谈谈这趟任务。专业的回应是什么？

options.en: Explain that the emergency department raised no concerns at the time, so the decision was sound
options.zh: 解释急诊科当时没有提出任何异议，说明这个决定在临床上是没有问题的

options.en: Say you cannot recall the call well enough to comment, and suggest the review be closed
options.zh: 表示对那趟任务已经记不清，无法评论，建议就此结束审查

options.en: Point out that the patient walked into the ED and was discharged, which shows no harm was done
options.zh: 指出患者是自己走进急诊并已出院的，说明并未造成伤害

options.en: Own the decision, walk through your assessment and reasoning honestly, and help identify fixes
options.zh: 承认决定是你做的，如实复盘当时的评估与判断，并配合找出需要改进之处

questions.explanationEn: Accountability means owning every decision made in practice — including one under review — and engaging honestly so the review can do its job. A is wrong because the ED's silence is not validation; they may not have known the mechanism, and the prehospital decision remains yours. B is wrong because claiming poor memory avoids the review, and your patient care record exists precisely so the call can be reconstructed. C is wrong because a good outcome does not make a departure from the standard of care correct; a lucky result is not a justification.
questions.explanationZh: 问责意味着为执业中的每个决定负责——包括正在被审查的决定——并如实配合，让审查发挥作用。A 错：急诊没提异议不等于认可，他们可能并不了解受伤机制，而院前决定的责任仍在你身上。B 错：推说记不清是在回避审查，患者照护记录的意义正是让这趟任务可以被还原。C 错：结果好不能证明偏离照护标准的决定是对的，侥幸不是理由。

questions.questionEn: During an interfacility transfer, the sending nurse hands you a syringe of the patient's IV antibiotic and says, “Just push this halfway through the trip so the schedule isn't delayed — it's already drawn up.” Your PCP licence and protocols do not authorize you to give IV antibiotics. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一次院间转运中，转出方护士递给你一支已抽好的患者静脉抗生素，说：“路上过半时帮忙推一下，别耽误给药时间——都抽好了。”你的 PCP 执照和规程并不授权你给静脉抗生素。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Give it as asked, since it is the patient's own prescribed drug and a nurse has directed it
options.zh: 照做——这是患者自己的处方药，而且是护士交代你给的

options.en: Decline, explain your licence does not authorize it, and agree on another plan, such as dosing first
options.zh: 拒绝并说明执照不授权此操作，同时商量替代方案，如出发前先给药

options.en: Give it, but document clearly that the nurse instructed you, so responsibility rests with her
options.zh: 照做给药，但清楚记录这是护士的指示，让责任由她承担

options.en: Take the syringe along unopened and hand it to the receiving staff, so they can give the dose on arrival
options.zh: 把注射器原封不动带上，到达后交给接收机构的工作人员，由他们按时给药

questions.explanationEn: You must work within the practice your licence authorizes no matter who asks; a nurse's instruction cannot extend it. Solving the problem with the sending team — giving the dose before departure, arranging a nurse escort, or adjusting the timing with the ordering physician — keeps the therapy on track without crossing that line. A is wrong because neither the patient's prescription nor the nurse's request authorizes you. C is wrong because documenting who asked does not transfer your accountability for an unauthorized act. D is wrong because carrying a syringe someone else drew up for a third person to give later is a medication-safety risk, and it leaves the timing problem unsolved.
questions.explanationZh: 无论是谁提出要求，你都只能在执照授权的范围内执业；护士的指示无法扩大这个范围。和转出方一起解决问题——出发前先给药、安排护士随车，或请开医嘱的医生调整给药时间——既能保证治疗不中断，也不越界。A 错：患者的处方和护士的要求都不能替代对你的授权。C 错：记录是谁让你做的，并不能转移你实施未授权操作的责任。D 错：带着别人抽好的药交给第三方稍后再给，本身就存在用药安全风险，而且给药时机的问题依然没有解决。

questions.questionEn: You explain to an alert, capable 45-year-old man why he needs IV access, and he holds out his arm. As you prepare the site, he says, “Actually, I don't want that.” What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你向一名神志清楚、具备决定能力的 45 岁男性解释了为什么要建立静脉通路，他随即伸出了手臂。你正在准备穿刺部位时，他说：“算了，我不想打了。”你应该怎么做？

options.en: Continue, because holding out his arm gave valid consent that covers a procedure once begun
options.zh: 继续操作——他伸出手臂就已给出有效同意，操作一旦开始就都涵盖在内

options.en: Stop, ask about his concern, explain the risks of going without IV access, and respect his choice
options.zh: 停下来，了解他的顾虑，说明不建立静脉通路的风险，并尊重他的决定

options.en: Continue while reassuring him, since a brief change of mind from needle anxiety is not a refusal
options.zh: 一边安抚一边继续，因为怕针引起的一时反悔并不算真正拒绝

options.en: Stop only once he has signed a refusal form, because a verbal withdrawal is not valid on its own
options.zh: 等他签了拒绝单再停手，因为口头撤回同意本身不具效力

questions.explanationEn: Valid consent must be voluntary, informed, specific, and given by a capable person — and a capable patient may withdraw it or refuse any part of care at any time. Stopping, exploring his concern, and explaining the risks makes his decision an informed one. A is wrong because consent given by conduct is still revocable; it is not a contract that locks him in. C is wrong because continuing after a capable patient says no is treatment without consent, which can amount to assault or battery whatever the reason for his change of mind. D is wrong because a refusal takes effect when he says it; you stop at once and document, and a signature never replaces the informed discussion.
questions.explanationZh: 有效的同意必须是自愿的、知情的、针对具体操作的，并由有决定能力的人作出——而有决定能力的患者可以随时撤回同意，或拒绝部分处置。停下来、了解他的顾虑并说明风险，才能让他的决定成为知情的决定。A 错：用行动表示的同意同样可以撤回，它不是一份把患者锁死的合同。C 错：有决定能力的患者已经说“不”还继续操作，就是未经同意的治疗，不管他为什么改变主意，都可能构成攻击或殴打（assault and battery）。D 错：拒绝在他说出口时就已生效，你应立即停手并记录；签字永远不能取代知情沟通本身。

questions.questionEn: A patient you transported twice last month finds your personal social media account, sends a friendly message thanking you, and asks if you would like to meet for coffee. What is the appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 一位上个月你转运过两次的患者找到了你的个人社交媒体账号，发来友好的感谢消息，并问你愿不愿意出来喝杯咖啡。恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Meet once for coffee as a kindness, keeping the conversation general and well away from her medical care
options.zh: 出于善意和她见一次面喝杯咖啡，只聊泛泛的话题，绝不谈她的病情

options.en: Reply politely and keep chatting online now and then, as long as you never meet in person
options.zh: 礼貌回复，偶尔在网上聊聊，只要不见面就行

options.en: Block the account without replying and tell no one, so the contact simply ends there
options.zh: 不回复直接拉黑，也不告诉任何人，让联系就此结束

options.en: Decline politely, avoid personal contact with the patient, and tell your supervisor if it continues
options.zh: 礼貌婉拒，避免与患者私下往来，如对方持续联系就告知主管

questions.explanationEn: Professional boundaries continue after the call: the power imbalance in a care relationship makes a personal relationship with a patient inappropriate, especially one you may treat again. A courteous decline sets the boundary clearly, and telling a supervisor about persistent contact protects both of you. A is wrong because even one social meeting turns a care relationship into a personal one. B is wrong because ongoing online chat is a personal relationship too, just in a different place. C is wrong because silent blocking leaves the patient confused about where the line is and leaves no record if the contact escalates.
questions.explanationZh: 职业边界在任务结束后依然存在：照护关系中的权力不对等，使得与患者——尤其是你以后可能还会出诊的患者——建立私人关系并不恰当。礼貌的婉拒能把界限讲清楚，对方持续联系时告知主管则能同时保护你和患者。A 错：哪怕只见一次面，也会把照护关系变成私人关系。B 错：持续网聊同样是私人关系，只是换了个场合。C 错：一声不吭直接拉黑，患者不知道界限在哪里，一旦事态升级也没有任何记录。

questions.questionEn: A 16-year-old with well-controlled asthma had a mild attack at school that fully resolved with her own inhaler before your arrival. Her vitals and exam are normal. She calmly explains her condition, her medications, and why she prefers to see her own doctor rather than go to hospital. Her parents cannot be reached, and the school insists you must transport because "she's a minor." What is the best course of action?
questions.questionZh: 一名哮喘控制良好的 16 岁学生在学校发作了一次轻度哮喘，在你们到达前已用自己的吸入器完全缓解。她的生命体征和查体均正常。她冷静地说明了自己的病情、用药情况，以及为什么更愿意去看自己的家庭医生而不是去医院。家长联系不上，校方坚持"她是未成年人"，必须转运。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Transport her anyway, because in BC no one under 19 may refuse care unless a parent agrees
options.zh: 无论如何都转运——在 BC 省，未满 19 岁的人除非家长同意，否则不能拒绝治疗

options.en: Assess her capacity; if she understands her condition and the risks of refusing, accept her informed refusal
options.zh: 评估她的决定能力；如果她理解自己的病情和拒绝的风险，就接受她的知情拒绝

options.en: Ask the school principal to sign the refusal on the parents' behalf, since the school is responsible for her today
options.zh: 请校长代表家长在拒绝单上签字，因为此刻学校对她负有责任

options.en: Stay on scene with her until a parent can be reached, however long that takes, before deciding
options.zh: 不管等多久都留在现场陪她，联系上家长之前不做任何决定

questions.explanationEn: Under the mature minor rule, a minor who fully appreciates the nature and consequences of a treatment decision may consent to it or refuse it; capacity, not a fixed age, is the test. For a resolved, familiar, low-risk episode with normal findings, a capable 16-year-old can decline transport — document her capacity, complete the informed refusal with clear return advice, and keep trying to reach her parents. A is wrong because there is no blanket age rule: BC's age of majority is 19, but a capable minor can still make this decision. C is wrong because a principal has no legal authority to consent or refuse on a student's behalf. D is wrong because holding the scene indefinitely neither respects her decision nor adds to her safety, and it ties up an ambulance.
questions.explanationZh: 根据 mature minor（成熟未成年人）规则，充分理解治疗决定的性质和后果的未成年人可以同意或拒绝该治疗；判断标准是决定能力，而不是固定年龄。对于一次已缓解、她本人熟悉、低风险且查体正常的发作，具备决定能力的 16 岁患者可以拒绝转运——记录她的决定能力，完成知情拒绝流程并给出明确的再次呼叫建议，同时继续设法联系家长。A 错：并不存在一刀切的年龄规则——BC 省成年年龄是 19 岁，但有决定能力的未成年人仍然可以作出这个决定。C 错：校长没有替学生同意或拒绝治疗的法定权力。D 错：无限期滞留现场既不尊重她的决定，也不会让她更安全，还白白占用一辆救护车。

questions.questionEn: At the end of a brutal night shift, your partner hands you the equipment checklist and says: "Just sign off the airway kit — I checked it yesterday, it's fine. Let's get out of here." You have not checked it yourself. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一个极度疲惫的夜班结束时，搭档把装备核查单递给你说："气道包直接签了吧——我昨天查过，没问题。赶紧走人。"你自己并没有检查过。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Sign it — routine checks rarely find problems, and your partner is very reliable
options.zh: 签了——例行检查很少发现问题，而且搭档一向很靠谱

options.en: Sign it now and plan to do the actual check yourself at the first standby point
options.zh: 先签字，打算到第一个待命点再亲自补做检查

options.en: Decline to sign for a check you did not perform, and do the check now even though you are both tired
options.zh: 拒绝为自己没有做过的检查签字，即使两人都很疲惫也现在就把检查做完

options.en: Sign it, but write “as per partner” beside your signature so the record shows who actually did the check
options.zh: 签字，但在签名旁注明“依据搭档所述”，表明实际是谁检查的

questions.explanationEn: Your signature is a professional attestation that you verified the equipment yourself — signing for a check you did not do is a false declaration, whatever qualifiers you add. The airway kit is life-critical: the next crew and the next patient rely on that attestation being true. A is wrong because your partner's reliability does not make your signature true. B is wrong because the record is false the moment you sign, and the promised check may never happen if a call comes in first. D is wrong because adding “as per partner” still certifies a check under your name that you did not perform.
questions.explanationZh: 你的签名是一项职业声明，表明你亲自核实过装备——为没做过的检查签字就是虚假声明，加什么备注都改变不了。气道包关乎生命，下一组人员和下一位患者都依赖这份声明是真的。A 错：搭档再靠谱，也不能让你的签名变成真的。B 错：签字的那一刻记录就已经是假的，而且一来任务，说好的检查可能根本做不成。D 错：注明“依据搭档所述”，仍然是以你的名义证明了一项你没做过的检查。

questions.questionEn: You arrive at a chest pain call. The patient's adult son meets you at the door, yelling that you took too long and blocking the hallway: "Twenty minutes! She could be dead!" What is the best initial response?
questions.questionZh: 你到达一个胸痛呼救现场。患者的成年儿子在门口拦住走廊对你吼叫："二十分钟！她可能已经死了！"最佳的初步应对是什么？

options.en: Tell him firmly that unless he moves aside now, you will call the police before going in
options.zh: 严正告诉他，如果现在不让开，你们就先叫警察再进去

options.en: Ignore the shouting, step around him, and go straight to the patient without engaging him
options.zh: 不理会吼叫，绕过他直接走向患者，完全不和他交涉

options.en: Stay calm, acknowledge his fear in a sentence, and ask him to take you to his mother right away
options.zh: 保持冷静，用一句话承接他的担心，然后请他马上带你去见他母亲

options.en: Have your partner walk him outside to calm down first, then go in and assess the patient
options.zh: 先让搭档把他带到屋外冷静一下，然后再进去评估患者

questions.explanationEn: Briefly acknowledging his fear and immediately giving him a job — leading you to his mother — is the fastest, safest de-escalation: you do not argue about response times, you do not get angry yourself, and he becomes an ally instead of an obstacle. A is wrong because threatening police as an opening move usually escalates someone who is already angry; police are for when calming fails or the scene becomes unsafe. B is wrong because pushing past an agitated person invites a physical confrontation and leaves him behind you, uncontrolled. D is wrong because removing him before trying to talk him down is premature, takes your partner away from the patient, and loses a family member who can give history.
questions.explanationZh: 用一句话承接他的恐惧，再马上交给他一件事做——带你去见他母亲——这是最快也最安全的降级方式：不就响应时间争论，自己也不动气，还把他从障碍变成帮手。A 错：一开口就拿警察威胁，往往会激怒本已愤怒的人；叫警察应留到劝不住或现场不安全的时候。B 错：硬从情绪激动的人身边挤过去，容易引发肢体冲突，还把一个失控的人留在了身后。D 错：还没尝试言语安抚就把他带走为时过早，既让搭档离开了患者，也失去了一位能提供病史的家属。

questions.questionEn: A middle-aged man tells you "I'm fine, really" — but he is pale, sitting very still, guarding his abdomen with one arm, and avoiding eye contact. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一名中年男子告诉你"我真的没事"——但他脸色苍白、坐着一动不动、一只手护着腹部、回避目光接触。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Gently name the mismatch — “You say you're fine, but you look uncomfortable” — and ask open questions
options.zh: 温和地点出言行不一——“你说没事，但看上去挺难受的”——再用开放式问题了解

options.en: Accept his answer, since he is alert and capable, and document “patient denies pain” in your report
options.zh: 接受他的回答，毕竟他神志清楚、有决定能力，并在报告中清楚记录“患者否认疼痛”

options.en: Tell him directly that he is clearly not fine and needs to be transported to hospital immediately
options.zh: 直截了当地告诉他明显有问题，必须马上送医

options.en: Ask his wife privately to persuade him to admit how much pain he is really in before you go on
options.zh: 私下请他妻子劝他承认到底有多疼，然后你再继续

questions.explanationEn: Pallor, guarding, stillness, and avoided eye contact often say more than words; recognizing and responding to them is a core communication skill. Naming the mismatch respectfully invites him to open up while leaving him in control. B is wrong because being alert and capable does not make his denial an accurate history — documenting “denies pain” alone ignores what his body is showing you. C is wrong because confronting him and ordering transport before you have assessed him shuts the conversation down. D is wrong because working through his wife goes around him and undermines his trust in you.
questions.explanationZh: 苍白、护腹、僵坐、回避目光，这些非语言表现传递的信息往往比言语更多；识别并回应它们是核心沟通能力。有礼貌地点出言行不一，既能邀请他敞开心扉，又让他保有主动权。B 错：神志清楚、有决定能力，并不代表他的否认就是准确的病史——只记一句“否认疼痛”等于无视他身体发出的信号。C 错：还没评估就正面对峙、命令他送医，会让对话直接中断。D 错：通过妻子施压是绕开患者本人，会破坏他对你的信任。

questions.questionEn: A woman has collapsed in a busy mall food court. She is now conscious and embarrassed; a crowd has gathered and several people are filming on their phones. How should you manage the environment?
questions.questionZh: 一名女性在繁忙的商场美食广场晕倒。她现在已恢复意识但很难为情；周围聚了一圈人，好几个人在用手机拍摄。你应该如何处理现场环境？

options.en: Complete your full assessment where she is lying, since moving her before assessing wastes time
options.zh: 就地完成全部评估，评估之前就搬动她只会浪费时间

options.en: Shield her, have security move the crowd back, expose only what you must, and finish in the ambulance
options.zh: 为她遮挡，请保安疏散人群，只暴露必需的部位，详细检查到救护车上再做

options.en: Move her to a private room straight away, before any assessment, so she is out of public view and calmer
options.zh: 在做任何评估之前，立刻把她转移到私密房间，让她避开众人目光、情绪平复下来

options.en: Ask the bystanders to stop filming and delete their videos before you begin assessing her
options.zh: 先要求围观者停止拍摄并删除视频，然后再开始评估她

questions.explanationEn: Protecting dignity and privacy runs alongside clinical care, not instead of it: shield her, control the crowd, expose only what the assessment needs, and do the detailed exam in the ambulance. A is wrong because a full exam in a public food court, in front of cameras, ignores her dignity when a better option is seconds away. C is wrong because she has just collapsed — moving her before even a primary assessment could miss instability. D is wrong because you cannot enforce deletion, and arguing with bystanders delays care; your bodies and security can block the view instead.
questions.explanationZh: 保护尊严和隐私应与临床照护同步进行，而不是取而代之：为她遮挡、控制人群、只暴露评估所需的部位，详细检查到救护车上再做。A 错：明明几秒钟就能换个地方，却在美食广场当着镜头做全身检查，无视了她的尊严。C 错：她刚刚晕倒过，连初步评估都不做就搬动，可能漏掉病情不稳定的征象。D 错：你无权强制别人删视频，和围观者交涉只会拖延照护；用身体和保安挡住视线就够了。

questions.questionEn: An 84-year-old woman with significant hearing loss is not understanding your questions. Her hearing aids are on the bedside table. Her daughter keeps answering for her. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一位有明显听力损失的 84 岁老太太听不懂你的提问。她的助听器放在床头柜上。她女儿不停地替她回答。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Speak louder and more slowly, raising your voice step by step until she starts to respond
options.zh: 说得更大声、更慢，一点点提高音量，直到她有反应

options.en: Direct your questions to the daughter, who knows her well, to save time and spare her frustration
options.zh: 改问熟悉她情况的女儿，既能节省时间，也免得老人一遍遍听不清、心里着急

options.en: Skip the history and rely on your physical exam findings, since communication is not working
options.zh: 既然沟通不畅，就跳过问诊，只依靠体格检查发现

options.en: Help her put in her hearing aids, face her in good light, speak clearly, and write key words
options.zh: 帮她戴上助听器，在光线好处与她面对面清楚地说，必要时写下关键词

questions.explanationEn: Adapting to her needs means restoring her ability to take part: hearing aids in, face-to-face in good light so she can see your lips, clear speech at a moderate pace, and written key words if needed — with the daughter only filling gaps. A is wrong because shouting distorts sound and strips dignity; turning up the volume does not fix a communication barrier. B is wrong because talking past her to the daughter removes her from her own care when she can still answer for herself. C is wrong because abandoning the history throws away information that simple adjustments could have obtained; never assume you cannot talk with a patient until you have tried.
questions.explanationZh: 适应她的需要，就是先恢复她参与的能力：戴上助听器，在光线充足处与她面对面（方便她看你的口型），语速适中、吐字清晰，必要时写下关键词——女儿只在需要时补充。A 错：喊叫会让声音失真，也有损尊严；提高音量解决不了沟通障碍。B 错：她自己还能回答，却绕过她去问女儿，等于把她排除在自己的照护之外。C 错：放弃问诊会丢掉本来稍作调整就能获得的信息；在真正尝试之前，永远不要认定无法和患者沟通。

questions.questionEn: En route to a familiar address, your senior partner sighs: "It's just Doris again — monthly anxiety call, in and out in ten minutes." On arrival, Doris tells you her chest feels tight and "different from my usual panic." What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 前往一个熟悉的地址途中，资深搭档叹气说："又是 Doris——每月一次的焦虑发作，十分钟搞定。"到达后，Doris 告诉你她胸口发紧，"和我平时的惊恐发作不一样"。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Reassure Doris that this is most likely her usual anxiety, and coach her breathing to settle it
options.zh: 安抚 Doris，说这多半还是她平时的焦虑，并引导她调整呼吸让症状平复

options.en: Set the label aside and fully assess today's complaint, treating “different” as a red flag
options.zh: 抛开标签，对今天的主诉做完整评估，把“这次不一样”当作危险信号

options.en: Let your partner lead the call, since he knows her history and usual presentation far better
options.zh: 让搭档主导这趟任务，因为他比你更了解她的病史和平时的表现

options.en: Do a focused assessment based on her known pattern, and reassess only if she fails to settle
options.zh: 按她既往的发作模式做针对性评估，只有症状不缓解时才重新评估

questions.explanationEn: Recognizing when a provider's bias may affect care — and correcting for it — is an explicit competency. Familiarity breeds anchoring, patients with anxiety still have heart attacks, and a patient saying “this feels different” is a classic warning sign. A is wrong because reassurance before assessment lets the label make the diagnosis. C is wrong because it hands the call to the very person whose bias is showing. D is wrong because building the assessment around her “known pattern” is the anchoring error itself; waiting to see whether she settles can delay recognition of a cardiac cause.
questions.explanationZh: 识别照护者自身的偏见可能影响照护质量并加以纠正，本身就是一项明确的能力要求。熟悉会带来锚定偏差，有焦虑病史的人同样会心梗，而患者说“这次感觉不一样”正是经典的警示信号。A 错：评估之前先安抚，等于让标签替你下了诊断。C 错：这是把任务交给偏见正在显露的那个人。D 错：围绕她的“既往模式”来设计评估，本身就是锚定错误；等着看症状会不会缓解，可能延误对心源性病因的识别。

questions.questionEn: An elderly man with mild confusion gives you a vague history. His daughter is present and says she manages his medications. How should you gather the history?
questions.questionZh: 一位有轻度意识混乱的老先生只能给出模糊的病史。他的女儿在场，并表示平时由她管理父亲的用药。你应该如何采集病史？

options.en: Interview the daughter alone in another room, so the patient does not become agitated
options.zh: 到另一个房间单独询问女儿，免得患者情绪激动

options.en: Decline the daughter's input to protect his privacy, and rely on what he can tell you
options.zh: 为保护他的隐私拒绝女儿提供信息，只依靠他本人能说的内容

options.en: With his permission, involve his daughter while keeping him engaged, and check the pill bottles
options.zh: 征得他同意后请女儿参与，同时让他本人保持参与，并对照实际药瓶核实

options.en: Base the medication history on the bottles you find, since his account and his daughter's may conflict
options.zh: 只依据现场找到的药瓶确定用药史，因为他和女儿的说法可能互相矛盾、说不清

questions.explanationEn: The competency is to seek and combine information from family and the circle of care — with the patient's consent — while keeping the patient at the centre. His account, his daughter's knowledge, and the actual bottles together give the most accurate picture. A is wrong because interviewing her separately sidelines him and denies him a say in what is shared about him. B is wrong because refusing input from the person who manages his medications throws away key information that he can consent to share. D is wrong because bottles show what was prescribed, not what he actually takes or what changed recently — that comes from people.
questions.explanationZh: 这项能力要求在征得患者同意的前提下，向家属和照护圈收集并整合信息，同时始终让患者处于中心位置。把他本人的叙述、女儿掌握的情况和实际药瓶结合起来，才能得到最准确的全貌。A 错：单独问女儿等于把他撇在一边，他也无从决定别人怎样谈论他。B 错：拒绝听取管理他用药的人提供的信息，会丢掉关键内容，而这些信息只要他同意就可以分享。D 错：药瓶只能说明开了什么药，说明不了他实际怎么吃、最近有什么变化——这些要靠人来告诉你。

questions.questionEn: After explaining a care plan, what is the most reliable way to confirm that a patient has actually understood the information?
questions.questionZh: 解释完照护计划后，确认患者是否真正理解信息的最可靠方法是什么？

options.en: Ask "Do you understand?" and accept a yes
options.zh: 问"你听明白了吗？"，对方说明白就行

options.en: Repeat the explanation a second time, more slowly
options.zh: 把解释再放慢重复一遍

options.en: Provide a written pamphlet covering the same information
options.zh: 提供一份包含相同信息的书面宣传单

options.en: Ask the patient to explain the plan back to you in their own words
options.zh: 请患者用自己的话把这个计划复述给你听

questions.explanationEn: The teach-back technique is the only option that verifies comprehension rather than assuming it: if the patient can restate the plan in their own words, they understood; gaps become immediately visible and correctable. Patients frequently answer "yes" out of politeness or embarrassment, repetition does not test uptake, and pamphlets fail anyone with limited literacy.
questions.explanationZh: 复述确认法（teach-back）是唯一能验证而非假定理解的选项：患者若能用自己的话复述计划，说明真正理解了；理解缺口也会立刻显现并可当场纠正。患者常出于礼貌或难为情而回答"明白"，重复讲解并不能检验吸收程度，宣传单对读写能力有限的人则毫无作用。

questions.questionEn: While moving an elderly patient through a narrow doorway, the stretcher tips and her forearm strikes the frame hard. A bruise is already forming. She and her son did not see exactly what happened. What must you do?
questions.questionZh: 通过狭窄门口搬运一位老年患者时，担架发生倾斜，她的前臂重重撞上门框，淤青已经开始显现。她和她儿子都没看清刚才发生了什么。你必须怎么做？

options.en: Tell them factually what happened and apologize, care for the injury, document it, and report it
options.zh: 如实告诉患者和她儿子经过并道歉，处理伤情、记录并上报

options.en: Assess and dress the bruise, and chart “bruise noted on right forearm” without stating the cause
options.zh: 评估并处理淤青，记录“右前臂见淤青”，但不写原因

options.en: Report it quietly to the receiving nurse, but spare the patient and her son the distressing details
options.zh: 悄悄告知接收护士，但不让患者和她儿子知道这些令人不安的细节

options.en: File an incident report, but explain what happened only if the family asks how the bruise occurred
options.zh: 提交事件报告，但只有家属问起淤青怎么来的时候才说明经过

questions.explanationEn: Disclosing harmful patient safety incidents accurately and appropriately to patients and families is an explicit obligation; it does not depend on being asked or on whether anyone saw it, and mistakes in care must never be concealed. Honest disclosure with an apology, care of the injury, accurate documentation, and an incident report maintain trust and let the system learn. B is wrong because charting the bruise without its cause is concealment in an official record. C is wrong because telling staff while keeping the patient and family in the dark withholds information they are entitled to. D is wrong because disclosure is not conditional on a question, and an internal report does not replace telling the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 向患者和家属准确、恰当地披露造成伤害的患者安全事件是一项明确的义务——不取决于对方有没有问、有没有人看见，照护中的失误也绝不能隐瞒。如实告知并道歉、处理伤情、准确记录并上报，才能维系信任、让系统吸取教训。B 错：只记淤青不写原因，是在正式记录里隐瞒。C 错：只告诉医护人员、却瞒着患者和家属，剥夺了他们有权知道的信息。D 错：披露不以对方提问为前提，内部上报也不能代替向患者本人说明。

questions.questionEn: The emergency department is overcrowded. The triage nurse asks for your report while you are standing in a hallway lined with other patients and visitors. Your patient has a psychiatric history relevant to the presentation. How should you give the report?
questions.questionZh: 急诊科人满为患。分诊护士让你就在挤满其他患者和探视者的走廊里交班。你的患者有一段与本次发病相关的精神科病史。你应该如何交班？

options.en: Give the full report, psychiatric history included, right where you are — handover cannot wait
options.zh: 就地完整交班，包括精神科病史——交接不能等

options.en: Hand over only the written report and skip the verbal one, so nothing is said aloud in the hallway
options.zh: 只递交书面报告、省略口头交班，这样走廊里就不会说出任何内容

options.en: Politely decline to hand over until a private room is free, so the report can be given properly
options.zh: 礼貌地表示要等有空的私密房间再交接，以便正规地交班

options.en: Step aside with the nurse, give the essentials quietly, and pass the sensitive history privately
options.zh: 和护士站到一旁，低声交代要点，敏感病史另找私密的方式传达

questions.explanationEn: Be careful where you talk about patients — even in hospital hallways, avoid conferring in front of bystanders. Respecting privacy does not mean withholding the information; it means controlling how and where you share it. A is wrong because announcing psychiatric history in a crowded hallway breaches confidentiality. B is wrong because skipping the verbal report removes the chance for questions and raises the risk that critical points are missed. C is wrong because refusing to hand over delays care for an indefinite time on an overcrowded night.
questions.explanationZh: 谈论患者时要注意场合——即使在医院走廊，也不要当着旁人讨论。尊重隐私不是不传递信息，而是控制传递的方式和场合。A 错：在挤满人的走廊里说出精神科病史就是泄密。B 错：省略口头交班，接收方就没有机会提问，关键信息被遗漏的风险也会增加。C 错：在人满为患的夜里拒绝交接，会让照护无限期地拖延。

questions.questionEn: A 52-year-old man with 40 minutes of pressure-like chest pain is alert and oriented but refuses transport: "I can't miss work, just give me the form to sign." What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一名 52 岁男性出现压迫样胸痛已 40 分钟，神志清楚、定向力正常，但拒绝转运："我不能耽误上班，把拒绝单给我签了吧。"最佳应对是什么？

options.en: Have him sign the refusal form right away, since a capable adult has every right to refuse care
options.zh: 立刻让他签拒绝单——有决定能力的成年人完全有权拒绝治疗

options.en: Tell him bluntly that he could die tonight, and refuse to leave until he agrees to come with you
options.zh: 直截了当地告诉他今晚可能会死，在他同意跟你走之前拒绝离开

options.en: Explore why he's refusing, explain the risks plainly, and if he still refuses, complete an informed refusal
options.zh: 了解拒绝原因，用通俗的话讲清风险；仍拒绝就完成知情拒绝流程

options.en: Ask police to attend and hold him for a capacity assessment, since his choice is putting his life at serious risk
options.zh: 请警察到场把他控制住做决定能力评估，因为他的选择已经严重危及生命

questions.explanationEn: A capable adult may refuse, but an informed refusal is a process, not a signature. Many patients with chest pain refuse out of fear or denial; finding out what is behind it, explaining that the ambulance cannot rule out a heart attack, offering a call with online medical oversight, and helping with practical barriers often changes the decision. If he still refuses, document capacity and the advice given, and make clear he can call back at any time. A is wrong because rushing to the form skips the “informed” part — a signature alone neither makes the refusal valid nor protects you. B is wrong because threats and refusing to leave are coercive and hostile. D is wrong because he is alert and oriented; there is no basis to detain a capable adult.
questions.explanationZh: 有决定能力的成年人可以拒绝，但知情拒绝是一个过程，而不是一个签名。不少胸痛患者是出于害怕或否认而拒绝；了解背后的原因、说明救护车上无法排除心梗、提议让他和在线医疗指导通话、帮他解决实际顾虑，往往能改变他的决定。若他仍坚持拒绝，就记录他的决定能力和你给出的建议，并明确告诉他随时可以再打电话。A 错：急着递单子跳过了“知情”这一步——光有签名既不能让拒绝有效，也保护不了你。B 错：恐吓、赖着不走属于强迫，态度也带有敌意。D 错：他神志清楚、定向力正常，没有任何理由扣留一位有决定能力的成年人。

questions.questionEn: You are transporting a stable Indigenous Elder from a small community to hospital. Before departure, the family asks for a few minutes so a community Elder can offer a prayer and smudge. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正要把一位病情稳定的原住民长者从小社区转运去医院。出发前，家属请求给几分钟时间，让社区长老做祈祷和烟熏净化仪式（smudge）。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Decline politely, explaining that transport times are fixed and the hospital is expecting you
options.zh: 礼貌拒绝，说明转运时间早就定好了，接收医院那边正等着你们按时到达

options.en: Make time for the ceremony, ask how to support it respectfully, and keep monitoring discreetly
options.zh: 为仪式留出时间，询问怎样支持才算尊重，同时不打扰地继续监测患者

options.en: Allow it only if it can be finished within two minutes, so the transfer schedule is not upset
options.zh: 只要两分钟内能完成就允许，以免打乱转运安排

options.en: Agree, and wait outside the room with your partner until the family calls you back in
options.zh: 同意，然后和搭档到房间外等候，直到家属叫你们回去

questions.explanationEn: Culturally safe care means supporting practices that matter to the patient and family in a respectful, non-judgmental way; for a stable patient a short ceremony creates no clinical conflict. Asking how to help shows humility, and quiet monitoring keeps the patient safe (if oxygen is running, agree on a safe arrangement with the family first). A is wrong because a booked transfer time is not a clinical reason to refuse something this important to a stable patient's family. C is wrong because an arbitrary time limit turns respect into a grudging concession. D is wrong because leaving the patient unmonitored abandons your duty — you can stay present respectfully.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全的照护，意味着以尊重、不评判的方式支持对患者和家人重要的习俗；对病情稳定的患者来说，简短的仪式与临床需要并不冲突。主动询问如何配合体现了谦逊，不打扰地监测则保障了患者安全（如果正在吸氧，先和家属商定安全的安排）。A 错：预约的转运时间不是临床理由，不足以拒绝一个对稳定患者家庭如此重要的仪式。C 错：武断地限定时间，会把尊重变成勉强的让步。D 错：离开患者不加监测是放弃职责——你完全可以尊重地留在现场。

questions.questionEn: A young woman is hyperventilating after a panic attack at her office. She keeps apologizing: "I'm so sorry, I'm wasting your time, I'm so stupid." Coworkers are watching. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一名年轻女性在办公室惊恐发作后过度换气。她不停道歉："真对不起，我在浪费你们的时间，我太蠢了。"同事们都在旁观。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Get to her eye level, tell her she was right to call, and coach her breathing while you assess
options.zh: 蹲到与她视线平齐，告诉她呼救是对的，边评估边引导她调整呼吸

options.en: Reassure her that nothing is physically wrong and that it is just anxiety, so she can relax
options.zh: 安慰她身体没有任何问题，只是焦虑而已，让她放轻松

options.en: Ask coworkers what happened while you quietly apply the monitor, so she isn't pressed to talk
options.zh: 一边默默连接监护仪，一边向同事了解经过，免得这时候逼她开口说话

options.en: Keep conversation to a minimum and transport quickly, so the hospital can assess her properly
options.zh: 尽量少说话、快速转运，让医院去好好评估

questions.explanationEn: A patient-centred approach builds trust through empathy and respect: telling her she was right to seek help counters the shame she is voicing, eye-level positioning reduces the power gap, and breath coaching combines care with assessment. B is wrong because calling it “just anxiety” before you have assessed her is premature — hyperventilation has other causes — and it belittles her. C is wrong because talking about her to coworkers while ignoring her deepens her embarrassment, and she is your best historian. D is wrong because minimal contact skips the assessment you are there to do and misses the reassurance that is itself part of treatment.
questions.explanationZh: 以患者为中心的方式靠共情和尊重建立信任：告诉她寻求帮助是对的，正好化解她流露出的羞耻感；与她视线平齐能缩小权力落差；呼吸引导则把照护与评估结合在一起。B 错：还没评估就说“只是焦虑”太草率——过度换气还有别的原因——而且有贬低之意。C 错：不理她、却去向同事打听她的情况，会让她更难为情，而她本人才是最好的病史来源。D 错：尽量少接触等于跳过了你本该完成的评估，也错过了本身就有治疗作用的安抚。

questions.questionEn: At a call for an elderly man with weakness, five family members crowd the room, all speaking at once and contradicting each other about his medications and when symptoms started. What is the best way to manage the encounter?
questions.questionZh: 一位老先生因乏力呼救，五名家属挤在房间里同时说话，对他的用药和症状开始时间各执一词。管理这次问诊的最佳方式是什么？

options.en: Ask everyone except the patient to leave the room immediately, so you can hear him clearly
options.zh: 立即请患者以外的所有人离开房间，好让你听清他说话

options.en: Let everyone speak and write down every version, then sort out the history on the way in
options.zh: 让每个人都说，把各种版本都记下来，在去医院的路上再慢慢理清病史

options.en: Direct your questions to the loudest relative, who seems to be the best informed about him
options.zh: 向嗓门最大、看上去最了解他情况的家属提问

options.en: Take charge politely: say you'll ask him first, then have one family member fill in details
options.zh: 礼貌地掌控节奏：说明先问患者本人，再请一位家属补充细节

questions.explanationEn: Providing a clear structure for the encounter is the competency here: patient first, then one organized source of collateral. This keeps him at the centre, turns noise into usable information, and keeps the family on side. A is wrong because sending everyone out loses the medication and onset information the family holds. B is wrong because unstructured input wastes time, and contradictory versions cannot reliably be sorted out later. C is wrong because volume is not accuracy, and it bypasses the patient entirely.
questions.explanationZh: 为整个问诊提供清晰的结构正是这项能力的体现：先问患者，再由一位家属有序补充。这样既让患者始终处于中心，又把嘈杂变成可用的信息，还能维持家属的配合。A 错：把所有人请出去，会丢掉家属掌握的用药和起病时间等信息。B 错：放任七嘴八舌既浪费时间，互相矛盾的说法事后也很难理清。C 错：嗓门大不代表说得准，而且完全绕开了患者本人。

questions.questionEn: While reviewing your submitted electronic patient care record, you notice you selected the wrong medication from a dropdown menu — the record shows a drug you never gave. What is the appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 复查已提交的电子患者照护记录时，你发现自己在下拉菜单里选错了药——记录上显示的是一种你根本没给过的药。恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Delete the record and create a fresh one without the error, so the chart is clean and accurate for the hospital
options.zh: 删除这份记录，重新建一份没有错误的，让交给医院的记录干净准确

options.en: Ask your supervisor to log in and correct the entry for you, since they have editing rights
options.zh: 请有编辑权限的主管登录系统替你更正

options.en: Amend it through the system so the change is tracked under your name, and tell the receiving facility
options.zh: 用系统的更正功能修改，让更改留痕在你名下，并通知接收机构

options.en: Leave it — dropdown errors are common, and the hospital will record what was actually given
options.zh: 不用管——下拉菜单选错很常见，医院会记录实际给了什么药

questions.explanationEn: A patient care record is a legal document: a correction must show when and why it was made, the original must never be destroyed, and only the author may revise it. Because a drug that was never given now appears on the record, the team relying on it must be told. A is wrong because deleting and recreating the record destroys the original and the audit trail. B is wrong because changes made by someone other than the author raise questions about the record's authenticity. D is wrong because the hospital only knows what you gave from your record — a false entry could lead them to withhold or repeat a medication.
questions.explanationZh: 患者照护记录是法律文件：更正必须注明时间和原因，原始记录绝不能销毁，而且只有记录的作者本人才能修改。由于记录上出现了一种根本没给过的药，必须告知正在依赖这份记录的团队。A 错：删掉重建会毁掉原始记录和审计痕迹。B 错：由作者以外的人修改，会让人质疑记录的真实性。D 错：医院只能从你的记录得知你给了什么药——一条错误的记录可能导致他们漏给或重复用药。

questions.questionEn: A patient with a minor complaint does not need transport tonight, but tells you he never knows where to get health advice when his clinic is closed. Which response best helps him manage his own health?
questions.questionZh: 一位轻症患者今晚不需要转运，但他告诉你，诊所关门后他从来不知道去哪里获取健康建议。哪种回应最能帮助他自我管理健康？

options.en: Show him how to reach the 24-hour nurse line (8-1-1 in BC) and pharmacists, and say when to call 911
options.zh: 教他用 24 小时护士热线（BC 是 8-1-1）和药剂师咨询，并讲清何时打 911

options.en: Suggest he look up his symptoms online when unsure, sticking to well-known health websites
options.zh: 建议他拿不准时上网查症状，只看知名的健康网站

options.en: Tell him advice lines are only for minor problems, so he should simply call 911 whenever he is worried
options.zh: 告诉他咨询热线只管小毛病，所以只要心里担心、拿不准，就直接打 911 叫救护车最稳妥

options.en: Leave a community resources pamphlet on the table for him to read later, without discussing it
options.zh: 把社区资源宣传单放在桌上让他以后看，不做讲解

questions.explanationEn: Helping patients identify, access, and use information and communication tools to manage their health is the competency here: concrete instructions on the nurse line and pharmacist advice, plus clear advice on when 911 is the right call, genuinely build his ability to cope after hours. B is wrong because a website cannot assess him or connect him with a clinician, and searching often misleads. C is wrong because sending every worry to 911 disempowers him and burdens the system; advice lines triage callers and direct them to emergency care when needed. D is wrong because an unexplained pamphlet is rarely read or acted on.
questions.explanationZh: 帮助患者识别、获取并使用信息与通讯工具来管理健康，正是这项能力的要求：具体教他使用护士热线和药剂师咨询，并讲清什么情况下才该打 911，才能真正提升他在诊所下班后的自我管理能力。B 错：网站无法评估他的情况，也不能让他联系上医护人员，自己搜索还常常误导人。C 错：事事都打 911 会削弱他的自我管理能力，也加重系统负担；咨询热线会分诊，需要时会让他去急诊。D 错：不加讲解的宣传单很少有人会去看、更少有人照着做。

questions.questionEn: Resuscitation of a 58-year-old man at home has been unsuccessful and efforts have been terminated. His wife is waiting in the kitchen with a neighbour. You must tell her. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 对一名 58 岁男性的家中复苏未能成功，抢救已终止。他的妻子和一位邻居在厨房等候。你必须告知她。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Soften the news with gentle words, such as “He has passed on — he's in a better place now”
options.zh: 用委婉的说法缓冲，比如“他已经走了——去了更好的地方”

options.en: Sit with her, warn that the news is bad, say clearly that Robert has died, then stay with her
options.zh: 坐到她身边，先说是坏消息，再清楚告诉她 Robert 已经去世，然后陪着她

options.en: Ask her family doctor to phone her with the news, since he knows her and her history better
options.zh: 请她的家庭医生打电话告知，因为医生更了解她和她的情况

options.en: First walk her through every intervention in detail, so she knows everything was tried, then tell her the outcome
options.zh: 先详细讲解你们做过的每一项抢救措施，让她知道大家尽了全力，最后再告诉她结果

questions.explanationEn: Death notification needs plain words: avoid euphemisms such as “passed away,” because the family needs to hear the word “dead” or “died.” A brief warning, clear language, a pause for her reaction, and continued presence — including helping arrange support such as the neighbour — form the accepted approach. A is wrong because euphemisms create confusion and false hope at the worst possible moment. C is wrong because you are the one there now; handing the news to someone else leaves her waiting and alone. D is wrong because front-loading clinical detail delays the truth she is waiting for — details can follow if she wants them.
questions.explanationZh: 告知死亡要用直白的语言：不要说“走了”“过世了”这类委婉语，家属需要听到“死亡”或“去世”这样明确的词。先简短预告是坏消息，再用清楚的语言告知，停下来给她反应的时间，并继续陪伴——包括帮她安排身边的支持，比如那位邻居——这是公认的做法。A 错：委婉语会在最糟糕的时刻制造困惑和虚假希望。C 错：此刻在她身边的是你，把告知推给别人只会让她独自干等。D 错：先大段讲解抢救细节，只会拖延她苦等的真相——细节可以等她想知道时再说。

questions.questionEn: You are handing over a chest pain patient. The receiving nurse keeps glancing at a monitor across the room, interrupts you twice, and starts walking away mid-report. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正在交接一名胸痛患者。接收护士不停瞟着房间另一头的监护仪，两次打断你，并在交班中途开始走开。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Hand her the written report and leave, since the patient has now become her responsibility
options.zh: 把书面报告交给她就走——患者现在已经归她负责了

options.en: Pause, ask politely for one minute of full attention, give the key points, and confirm she has them
options.zh: 停下来，礼貌地请她专注一分钟，交代关键要点，并确认她已经接收

options.en: Start the report again from the beginning, louder, so she cannot miss any of the details
options.zh: 提高音量从头再讲一遍，让她不可能漏掉任何细节

options.en: Find the charge nurse and complain about her conduct first, so it doesn't happen again, then finish the handover
options.zh: 先去找护士长投诉她的态度，然后再回来把交接正式做完，免得同样的事再发生

questions.explanationEn: A handover is complete only when the receiver has actually taken in the critical information, and the sender shares responsibility for making that happen. Asking for focused attention, compressing to the essentials, and closing the loop with confirmation adapts the handover to a busy room. A is wrong because care is not safely transferred if the critical information never landed — the paper may not be read in time. C is wrong because repeating everything louder to someone who is not listening changes nothing and wastes time. D is wrong because complaining before the patient is handed over inverts the priorities; any concern can be raised afterward through proper channels.
questions.explanationZh: 只有当接收方真正接收了关键信息，交接才算完成，而发送方对此负有共同责任。请对方专注片刻、压缩到最核心的要点、再通过确认形成闭环，就是针对繁忙环境调整交接方式。A 错：关键信息没有传达到位，照护就没有安全移交——书面报告未必能及时被看到。C 错：对一个没在听的人提高音量从头再讲，毫无作用，只会浪费时间。D 错：患者还没交接就先去投诉是本末倒置；有意见可以事后通过正规渠道反映。

questions.questionEn: In a rural BC area, you are transporting a COPD patient whose breathing is worsening despite your treatment. The hospital is 40 minutes away. Dispatch advises an ACP unit is available and could meet you along your route in about 15 minutes. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 在 BC 省的乡村地区，你正在转运一名 COPD 患者，尽管已给予处置，其呼吸仍在恶化。距医院还有 40 分钟车程。调度告知有一个 ACP（高级救护）单元可在约 15 分钟后与你们在转运路线上会合。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Request the intercept now, set a meeting point with dispatch, and keep transporting as you treat
options.zh: 立即请求中途会合，与调度约定会合点，同时边处置边继续转运

options.en: Continue alone to hospital, since transport is under way and arranging a meeting is a distraction
options.zh: 独自继续送往医院——反正已经在路上了，安排会合只会让你分心

options.en: Pull over and wait at the roadside for the ACP unit, so the patient gets advanced care sooner
options.zh: 靠边停车在路边等 ACP 单元，让患者更快得到高级处置

options.en: Ask dispatch to have the ACP crew meet you at the hospital, so no time is lost on the road
options.zh: 请调度安排 ACP 组员在医院与你们会合，路上不耽误时间

questions.explanationEn: Recognizing when care should move to a higher level — and acting early — is the competency: an en-route intercept brings advanced care to a deteriorating patient about 25 minutes sooner than the hospital would, without stopping progress toward definitive care. B is wrong because it gives up help that is available to a patient who is getting worse despite your treatment. C is wrong because waiting stationary throws away transport time when a moving rendezvous gives you both. D is wrong because meeting at the hospital defeats the purpose of an intercept — hospital care is waiting there anyway.
questions.explanationZh: 判断何时应把照护交给更高级别的人员，并尽早行动，正是这项能力的要求：途中会合能让病情恶化的患者比到院提前约 25 分钟得到高级处置，同时不中断向确定性治疗的推进。B 错：患者在处置下仍在恶化，却放弃了现成的支援。C 错：原地等待白白浪费了转运时间，而在路上会合可以两者兼得。D 错：在医院会合就失去了中途会合的意义——医院本来就有高级处置。

questions.questionEn: You arrive at a cardiac arrest where two firefighter first responders are performing good-quality CPR with an AED attached. How should you integrate them as you take over the call?
questions.questionZh: 你到达一个心搏骤停现场，两名消防急救先遣人员正在进行高质量 CPR，AED 已连接。接手任务时你应该如何整合他们？

options.en: Take over compressions yourself immediately, since you are now responsible for the arrest
options.zh: 既然骤停现在由你负责，就立即亲自接手胸外按压

options.en: Ask the firefighters to step back entirely so your own crew can run the resuscitation
options.zh: 请消防员完全退开，由你们组自己进行复苏

options.en: Keep the firefighters rotating on compressions while you two manage the AED, airway, and team
options.zh: 让消防员继续轮换按压，你和搭档负责 AED、气道和整个团队的协调

options.en: Have a firefighter run the AED while you and your partner take over and share compressions
options.zh: 让一名消防员负责操作 AED，你和搭档亲自接手，两人轮流做胸外按压

questions.explanationEn: Optimizing care through appropriate delegation means matching tasks to people: CPR-trained first responders are ideal for the physically demanding compression rotation, freeing the paramedics to manage the airway, the AED and rhythm checks, and the team as a whole. A is wrong because replacing an effective compressor for no clinical reason causes an avoidable interruption. B is wrong because sending away trained hands means your two-person crew will tire quickly and compressions will suffer. D is wrong because, although firefighters can operate an AED, putting both paramedics on compressions leaves no one leading the resuscitation or managing the airway.
questions.explanationZh: 通过恰当委派来优化照护，意味着把任务和人匹配起来：受过 CPR 训练的先遣人员最适合承担体力消耗大的按压轮换，从而让救护员腾出手来管理气道、操作 AED 和判读心律，并统筹整个团队。A 错：没有临床理由就换掉有效的按压者，只会造成本可避免的中断。B 错：把受过训练的人手赶走，你们两人很快会疲劳，按压质量随之下降。D 错：消防员虽然可以操作 AED，但让两名救护员都去按压，就没人主导复苏、也没人管理气道了。

questions.questionEn: Your patient has new facial droop and arm weakness that began 90 minutes ago and a positive FAST-VAN screen. You believe she meets your service's criteria to bypass the closer hospital for the designated stroke centre; your equally experienced partner wants to go to the closer community ED. How should this be resolved?
questions.questionZh: 你的患者 90 分钟前出现新发面部下垂和上肢无力，FAST-VAN 筛查阳性。你认为她符合机构的绕行标准，应越过较近的医院直送指定卒中中心；资历与你相当的搭档则想去更近的社区急诊。这个分歧应如何解决？

options.en: Talk it through briefly against the destination criteria; if still unsure, call online clinical support
options.zh: 对照转送标准简短讨论，如仍不确定就联系在线临床支持

options.en: Defer to your partner this time, since keeping the working relationship smooth matters on a long, busy shift
options.zh: 顺着搭档的意见，忙碌的班次里维持合作关系更重要

options.en: As the attending paramedic, set the destination yourself and move on without more discussion
options.zh: 既然你是主责救护员，就自己定下目的地，不再讨论

options.en: Ask the patient's family to choose between the two hospitals, since it affects them most
options.zh: 让家属在两家医院中选择，毕竟这个决定对他们和患者影响最大

questions.explanationEn: Respectful shared decision-making resolves clinical disagreement with evidence rather than hierarchy or harmony: the destination criteria are the objective referee, and online clinical support exists for exactly this kind of unresolved field question. B is wrong because silent deference may cost the patient time-critical stroke treatment. C is wrong because a unilateral decision discards a colleague's input and the chance to catch your own error. D is wrong because the destination is a clinical judgment; handing it to the family shifts a professional decision onto people without the information to make it.
questions.explanationZh: 尊重的共同决策靠证据而不是层级或和气来化解临床分歧：转送标准就是客观的裁判，而在线临床支持正是为这种现场悬而未决的问题设立的。B 错：沉默让步可能让患者错失时间敏感的卒中治疗。C 错：单方面拍板既抛开了同事的意见，也失去了发现自己判断失误的机会。D 错：去哪家医院是临床判断，交给家属决定等于把专业判断推给了不掌握相关信息的人。

questions.questionEn: At an assault scene, a police officer wants to interview your patient — who has facial injuries and a possible concussion — before you complete your assessment and transport. The officer says evidence is time-sensitive. How should you handle this?
questions.questionZh: 在一处袭击案现场，一名警察想在你完成评估和转运之前询问你的患者——患者面部受伤且可能有脑震荡。警察表示取证有时效性。你应该如何处理？

options.en: Let the interview go ahead first, then assess the patient once the officer has what he needs
options.zh: 先让警察问话，等他问完再评估患者

options.en: Tell the officer he has no authority at a medical scene and must step back until you have left with the patient
options.zh: 告诉警察他在医疗现场没有任何权限，必须退到一边，等你们带患者离开再说

options.en: Let the patient decide whether he would rather be interviewed before or after treatment
options.zh: 让患者自己决定是治疗前还是治疗后接受询问

options.en: Explain the patient needs assessment and transport now, and offer brief questions while you package
options.zh: 说明患者现在需要评估和转运，并提议在打包转运时让他问几个简短问题

questions.explanationEn: Managing differences with public safety colleagues means protecting the patient's clinical priority while respecting the officer's legitimate needs; offering concrete options — a few essential questions while you package, a full interview at the hospital — resolves the conflict instead of escalating it. A is wrong because delaying care for an injured, possibly concussed patient puts him at risk. B is wrong because ordering police away damages a working relationship you rely on, often for your own safety. C is wrong because a possibly concussed patient is not a reliable judge of this, and it leaves the disagreement unresolved.
questions.explanationZh: 与公共安全同事处理分歧，意味着在守住患者临床优先级的同时，尊重警方的正当需要；提出具体方案——打包转运时问几个必要问题，到医院再做完整询问——能化解冲突而不是激化矛盾。A 错：为了问话推迟照护，会让受伤且可能脑震荡的患者承担风险。B 错：命令警察离开会破坏你所依赖的协作关系，而你的安全往往也要靠他们。C 错：可能脑震荡的患者判断不可靠，而且分歧仍然没有解决。

questions.questionEn: You have just cleared the hospital when a neighbouring crew radios you directly: they have found a second patient at their scene two blocks away and need another unit. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你们刚在医院交接完毕，附近一个班组直接用无线电呼叫你们：他们在两个街区外的现场发现了第二名患者，需要另一个单元支援。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Tell them to route the request through dispatch and wait to be assigned
options.zh: 让他们走调度流程提请求，你们等候派遣

options.en: Confirm your availability with dispatch and respond promptly to assist
options.zh: 向调度确认你们可以出动，并迅速前往支援

options.en: Decline — your meal break is overdue and another unit can take it
options.zh: 婉拒——你们的用餐休息早就该开始了，让别的单元去

options.en: Drive straight over without notifying dispatch since it is only two blocks
options.zh: 反正只有两个街区，不通知调度直接开过去

questions.explanationEn: Responding appropriately to requests for help means acting on them promptly while keeping the system informed: confirming with dispatch takes seconds, keeps you visible in the deployment picture, and gets help moving. Bouncing a colleague's direct request back into a queue delays care; refusing for a break fails the team; and going off-grid means dispatch cannot track, support, or cover you.
questions.explanationZh: 恰当回应求助请求意味着迅速行动的同时让系统知情：向调度确认只需几秒钟，既让你们在调派全局中保持可见，又让支援立即启动。把同事的直接请求推回排队流程会延误照护；为了休息而拒绝辜负了团队；而脱离调度擅自行动则意味着调度无法追踪、支援或为你们补位。

questions.questionEn: At a two-car collision you are the attending paramedic. Present: your partner, two firefighters, and a bystander who identifies herself as an off-duty ICU nurse. Patient 1 is walking around; patient 2 is trapped and moaning. How do you coordinate the team?
questions.questionZh: 在一起两车相撞事故中你是主责救护员。现场有：你的搭档、两名消防员，以及一位自称是休班 ICU 护士的路人。患者 1 在四处走动；患者 2 被困车内、正在呻吟。你应如何协调团队？

options.en: Send everyone to the trapped patient, since his moaning suggests he is the most critically injured
options.zh: 让所有人都去处理被困患者，因为他的呻吟说明他伤得最重

options.en: Have the nurse manage the trapped patient alone while your whole crew assesses the patient who is walking
options.zh: 让护士独自负责被困患者，你们组去评估那位能走动的患者

options.en: Put your partner and a firefighter on the trapped patient, the nurse with the walking one, and coordinate
options.zh: 让搭档和一名消防员处理被困患者，护士陪同能走动的患者，你负责统筹

options.en: Treat the walking patient yourself first, since he is the easiest to reach, then reassess the scene
options.zh: 你先亲自处理能走动的患者，因为他最容易接触，处理完再重新评估整个现场

questions.explanationEn: Coordinating several team members in a complex scene means allocating each resource by acuity and ability while someone keeps overall command: your partner, with a firefighter's help, on the trapped patient; the off-duty nurse — once you have confirmed she is willing — watching the ambulatory patient and reporting changes; the other firefighter on scene hazards; and you coordinating. A is wrong because swarming one patient leaves the other unassessed, and walking does not mean uninjured. B is wrong because it gives primary responsibility for the sicker patient to an unverified bystander working outside your system. D is wrong because anchoring yourself to the easiest task means no one is coordinating the scene.
questions.explanationZh: 在复杂现场协调多名团队成员，意味着按伤情轻重和各人能力分配资源，同时有人统筹全局：搭档在一名消防员协助下处理被困患者；休班护士在你确认她愿意协助后，陪同能走动的患者并报告变化；另一名消防员负责现场危险；你负责统筹。A 错：全员扑向一名患者会让另一名无人评估，而能走动不代表没受伤。B 错：把较重患者的主责交给身份未经核实、又不在你们体系内的路人。D 错：你把自己拴在最轻松的任务上，现场就没人统筹了。

questions.questionEn: In the ED hallway, your partner mutters loudly enough for staff to hear: "Typical — nurses here never listen to a word we say." A nurse looks over. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 在急诊走廊里，你的搭档嘟囔的音量大得让工作人员都能听见："一贯如此——这里的护士从来不听我们说话。"一位护士看了过来。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Quietly agree with your partner, so he doesn't feel isolated in front of the hospital staff
options.zh: 小声附和搭档，免得他在医院员工面前孤立无援

options.en: Correct your partner on the spot in front of the ED staff, so they see you disagree with him
options.zh: 当着急诊员工的面立刻纠正搭档，让他们看到你并不认同

options.en: Report the comment to the regulator as unprofessional conduct, since the staff overheard it
options.zh: 既然员工都听到了，就把这句话作为不专业行为上报给监管机构

options.en: Don't join in, stay courteous with the staff, and talk to your partner privately afterward
options.zh: 不附和，继续对急诊员工以礼相待，事后私下和搭档谈谈

questions.explanationEn: Interacting respectfully includes not amplifying disrespect and dealing with it constructively. A private conversation afterward corrects the behaviour while preserving your partner's dignity and the team relationships you both depend on. A is wrong because joining in damages an interprofessional relationship you need every shift. B is wrong because correcting him publicly humiliates him and creates a second conflict in front of the same staff. C is wrong because a regulatory report is far out of proportion to a first rude remark; this is best handled peer to peer, escalating only if it becomes a pattern.
questions.explanationZh: 尊重地互动，既包括不为不敬言论推波助澜，也包括以建设性的方式处理它。事后私下沟通既能纠正行为，又保全了搭档的颜面，也维护了你们双方都依赖的团队关系。A 错：附和会破坏你们每个班次都要依赖的跨专业关系。B 错：当众纠正会让搭档难堪，还在同一群员工面前制造了第二个冲突。C 错：为一句失礼的话就上报监管机构严重失当；这类问题最适合同事之间解决，只有形成固定模式时才需要升级。

questions.questionEn: You respond to a palliative patient's home for increased pain. A home-care nurse is present, knows the patient well, and is following an established palliative care plan. How should you work with her?
questions.questionZh: 你出诊到一位安宁疗护患者家中处理疼痛加重。一名居家护理护士在场，她非常了解患者，并正在执行既定的安宁照护计划。你应该如何与她协作？

options.en: Briefly clarify roles: ask what she has done, review the care plan, and agree on who does what
options.zh: 简短厘清分工：问她做了什么，看照护计划怎么定，商定各自负责什么

options.en: Take over completely, since once 911 has been called the paramedic crew directs all of the care
options.zh: 全面接管——一旦有人拨打了 911，就该由救护组来主导所有的照护和决定

options.en: Leave the management to her entirely, since she knows the patient and the plan far better
options.zh: 既然她更了解患者和照护计划，就把处置完全交给她

options.en: Work in parallel to save time: you do your own assessment while she carries on with hers
options.zh: 为节省时间各干各的：你做你的评估，她继续她的

questions.explanationEn: This is exactly a situation of overlapping, shared responsibility: the nurse holds continuity, context, and the palliative care plan; you bring emergency assessment and transport. A short role-clarifying conversation merges the two into one coherent plan. B is wrong because a total takeover discards her knowledge and the patient's documented goals of care. C is wrong because deferring entirely abandons your duty to assess the patient you were called to. D is wrong because working in separate silos invites duplicated or contradictory interventions, such as two people giving the same medication.
questions.explanationZh: 这正是职责重叠、需要协商分工的情境：护士掌握连续性、背景信息和安宁照护计划；你带来急救评估和转运能力。一次简短的分工沟通，就能把两者合成一个连贯的方案。B 错：全盘接管会丢掉她掌握的情况和患者已经写明的照护目标。C 错：完全放手是放弃了你评估这位患者的职责——你正是为此被叫来的。D 错：各干各的容易出现重复或相互矛盾的处置，比如两个人给了同一种药。

questions.questionEn: You and your partner argued about a personal matter before shift. Now, managing an unstable patient, your partner is answering you in single words, and you just caught a miscommunication that nearly caused a missed treatment step. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 上班前你和搭档因私事争吵。现在处理一名不稳定患者时，搭档对你爱答不理，你刚刚发现一次沟通失误差点导致漏掉一个处置步骤。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Stop and settle the personal argument right now, so the two of you can work together properly
options.zh: 现在就停下来把私人矛盾说清楚，你们俩才能好好配合

options.en: Work around your partner and manage the patient largely on your own until the call is over
options.zh: 绕开搭档，基本靠自己一个人处理患者直到任务结束

options.en: Radio dispatch for a crew swap partway through the call, so the patient gets a calmer, functioning team
options.zh: 呼叫调度要求在任务中途换一个班组，让患者能有一个心平气和、配合默契的团队

options.en: Call a quick reset — “closed-loop from here on” — finish the call, then deal with the conflict after
options.zh: 做一次简短的状态重置——“从现在起指令都复诵”——完成任务后再处理矛盾

questions.explanationEn: When conflict starts degrading patient care, the immediate duty is to contain it: an explicit professional reset with closed-loop communication restores safety now, and the underlying conflict is dealt with after transfer of care — with a supervisor's help if you cannot resolve it together. A is wrong because hashing out a personal argument over an unstable patient pulls attention away from the patient. B is wrong because freezing out your partner removes half the crew and doubles the risk of missed steps. C is wrong because a mid-call crew change delays care and is impractical with an unstable patient.
questions.explanationZh: 当矛盾开始影响患者照护时，当务之急是控制住它：明确的状态重置加上闭环复诵沟通，能立即恢复安全；深层矛盾留到交接之后再处理，两人解决不了就请主管介入。A 错：在不稳定患者面前清算私人恩怨，会把注意力从患者身上拉走。B 错：冷落搭档等于少了半个班组，漏步骤的风险反而加倍。C 错：任务中途换组会延误照护，面对不稳定患者也根本不现实。

questions.questionEn: You are partnered with an ACP who is preparing an advanced intervention that your PCP licence does not authorize. Which form of assistance is appropriate for you to provide?
questions.questionZh: 你与一名 ACP（高级救护员）搭档，对方正准备实施一项你的 PCP 执照并不授权的高级操作。你提供哪种协助是恰当的？

options.en: Prepare and pass equipment, monitor the patient, and carry out tasks your own licence allows
options.zh: 准备和传递器械、监测患者，并执行你自己的执照所允许的操作

options.en: Perform the advanced procedure yourself under the ACP's direct verbal guidance and supervision
options.zh: 在 ACP 的直接口头指导和监督下，由你亲自实施这项高级操作

options.en: Decline any involvement in tasks connected to the advanced care, to stay clear of the procedure
options.zh: 拒绝参与任何与高级处置有关的工作，和这项操作完全撇清关系

options.en: Give the ACP-only drug yourself, as long as the ACP draws it up and double-checks the dose
options.zh: 只要 ACP 抽好药并复核剂量，就可以由你给这种 ACP 专属药物

questions.explanationEn: Helping a team member is expected — within each provider's authorized practice and ability. Preparing equipment, monitoring, and performing tasks your own licence allows make the team effective without crossing authorization lines. B is wrong because supervision by an ACP does not authorize you to perform a procedure your licence does not include. C is wrong because refusing all involvement fails the team and the patient when many supporting tasks are yours to do. D is wrong because administering the drug is the act that requires authorization; who drew it up or checked it does not change that.
questions.explanationZh: 配合团队成员的协助请求是应尽之责——但要在各自的执照授权和能力范围之内。准备器械、监测患者、执行你自己执照允许的操作，能让团队高效运转，又不越过授权的界线。B 错：有 ACP 监督，并不等于你获得了执照之外的操作授权。C 错：明明有很多辅助工作是你可以做的，拒绝一切参与会辜负团队和患者。D 错：需要授权的恰恰是“给药”这个动作，药是谁抽的、谁核对的，都改变不了这一点。

questions.questionEn: You treated a diabetic man's hypoglycemia with oral glucose. He is now fully alert (GCS 15), has eaten a meal, and a repeat glucose is normal. You recommend transport, as your protocol expects, but he declines. His wife will stay with him. When is it appropriate to leave him at home?
questions.questionZh: 你用口服葡萄糖（oral glucose）处理了一名糖尿病男性的低血糖。他现已完全清醒（GCS 15），吃过一顿饭，复测血糖正常。你按规程建议转运，但他拒绝了。他妻子会在家陪着他。在什么情况下让他留在家里才是恰当的？

options.en: Never — any patient who has received treatment from paramedics must be transported to hospital
options.zh: 任何情况都不行——凡是接受过救护员处置的患者都必须送医

options.en: Once he shows capacity, understands the risk of recurrence and when to call back, and you document it
options.zh: 当他展现出决定能力，理解复发风险和何时该再呼叫，并且你做好了记录时

options.en: Only if a police officer attends to witness him signing the refusal form, to protect the crew
options.zh: 只有警察到场见证他签拒绝单才可以，以保护出勤人员

options.en: As soon as he signs the refusal form, since the signature itself proves he has made an informed decision
options.zh: 只要他在拒绝单上签了字就可以，签名本身就说明他已作出决定

questions.explanationEn: BC's diabetic emergency protocol expects transport after treatment, so you recommend it — but a capable adult may still refuse. Capacity here means he is oriented, his glucose and oxygen saturation are normal, he understands his condition and the risk of the low sugar returning, and he has a reasonable plan: food eaten, follow-up with his doctor, his wife staying and knowing the warning signs and when to call back. Document all of it thoroughly. A is wrong because treatment does not remove a capable person's right to refuse; the protocol sets what you recommend, not a power to force him. C is wrong because an impartial witness helps if one is present, but police attendance is not a condition of a valid refusal. D is wrong because a signature without capacity and an informed discussion is not an informed refusal and protects no one.
questions.explanationZh: BC 考纲的糖尿病急症规程要求处置后转运，所以你应建议他去医院——但有决定能力的成年人仍然可以拒绝。这里的决定能力包括：定向力正常，血糖和血氧饱和度正常，理解自己的病情和低血糖再次发作的风险，并有合理的后续安排——已经进食、会去找自己的医生随访、妻子在家陪着并知道哪些征象要警惕、什么时候要再打电话。这些都要详细记录。A 错：接受过处置并不会剥夺有决定能力者拒绝的权利；规程规定的是你该建议什么，而不是授权你强制送医。C 错：在场有中立见证人固然好，但警察到场并不是拒绝有效的前提。D 错：没有决定能力评估和知情沟通的签名不算知情拒绝，保护不了任何人。

questions.questionEn: The ED is overwhelmed. The triage nurse glances at your elderly patient — who has new confusion and a fever — says "hallway six, we'll get to her," and walks away before you can give a report. No one has accepted care. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 急诊科忙得不可开交。分诊护士瞥了一眼你那位新发意识混乱伴发热的老年患者，丢下一句"六号走廊位，我们稍后处理"，没等你交班就走开了。没有任何人正式接手照护。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Move her to hallway six and leave, since responsibility transfers once she is inside the hospital
options.zh: 把她安置到六号走廊位就离开——人进了医院，责任就已经转移了

options.en: Wait ten minutes, then leave the paperwork at the triage desk and clear for your next call
options.zh: 等十分钟，把文书留在分诊台，然后清空待命接下一趟任务

options.en: Give your report to the ward clerk, so that at least someone in the department has the information you have
options.zh: 把交班内容告诉科室文员，这样至少科里有人掌握你手上关于她的这些信息

options.en: Stay with her, keep monitoring, and pursue a proper handover, escalating if the delay endangers her
options.zh: 留在她身边继续监测，坚持完成正规交接；如果拖延危及她，就逐级上报

questions.explanationEn: Care is not transferred until a qualified clinician accepts it along with the information needed to continue safely — a hallway assignment is not a handover. A confused, febrile older patient can deteriorate quietly, so you stay, monitor, and escalate to the charge nurse or your supervisor if needed. A is wrong because being physically inside the hospital does not transfer responsibility. B is wrong because timing out and leaving paperwork leaves her with no clinician who knows her story. C is wrong because a ward clerk is not a clinician and cannot accept care of a patient.
questions.explanationZh: 在具备资质的临床人员带着继续安全照护所需的信息正式接手之前，照护并没有转移——分一个走廊位不等于交接。意识混乱伴发热的老年患者可能在不知不觉中恶化，所以你要留下、监测，必要时升级找护士长或你的主管。A 错：人进了医院，并不代表责任就转移了。B 错：等够时间、丢下文书就走，会让她身边没有任何一个了解她病情的临床人员。C 错：科室文员不是临床人员，无法接手患者的照护。

questions.questionEn: During a long offload delay, the ED charge nurse snaps at you in front of colleagues: "You people keep dumping patients on us and my staff are drowning." You still have a moderately ill patient waiting on your stretcher. What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一次漫长的交接延误中，急诊护士长当着同事的面冲你发火："你们这些人不停地把患者甩给我们，我的人都快撑不住了。"你的担架上还躺着一位病情中等的患者等待交接。最佳回应是什么？

options.en: Stay professional: acknowledge the pressure, refocus on your patient's needs, and raise offload later
options.zh: 保持专业：承认她的压力，把注意力拉回患者身上，交接延误事后再反映

options.en: Point out calmly that the ED's staffing problems are not the ambulance service's fault or yours
options.zh: 平静地指出急诊人手不足不是救护车服务的错，也不是你的错

options.en: Report her outburst to hospital management first, then come back to complete the handover
options.zh: 先向医院管理层投诉她的失态，再回来完成交接

options.en: Apologize, then wait silently for as long as it takes, without raising your patient's needs with her again
options.zh: 向她道歉，然后不管要等多久都默默等着，再也不跟她提你那位患者的需要

questions.explanationEn: Resolving conflict during care means not taking the bait: acknowledging her very real pressure defuses the confrontation, keeping the focus on the patient serves the person you are both there for, and the systemic offload problem belongs in system-level channels afterward. B is wrong because arguing about fault, even if true, escalates the conflict in front of colleagues and the patient. C is wrong because complaining before the handover is done puts the grievance ahead of the patient. D is wrong because silent capitulation abandons your duty to advocate for the patient on your stretcher — if he worsens, someone must know.
questions.explanationZh: 在照护过程中化解冲突，关键是不接招：承认她面对的真实压力可以平息对抗，把焦点放在患者身上才是你们双方共同的职责，而系统性的交接延误问题应在事后通过系统层面的渠道反映。B 错：即使说的是事实，当着同事和患者争论谁的责任也只会升级冲突。C 错：交接还没完成就先去投诉，是把个人不满放在了患者前面。D 错：沉默妥协等于放弃为担架上的患者发声——万一他病情加重，总得有人知道。

questions.questionEn: A student paramedic on her second ride-along shift takes far too long to get IV access and misses the vein. The patient is stable. What is the most effective way to give feedback?
questions.questionZh: 一名实习救护学员在第二次跟车实习中建立静脉通路耗时过长且穿刺失败。患者情况稳定。给予反馈最有效的方式是什么？

options.en: Correct her technique at the bedside straight away, so the lesson lands while it is still fresh
options.zh: 当场在患者床边纠正她的手法，趁印象新鲜把要点讲透

options.en: Debrief privately soon after: ask how she thought it went, give specific points, and agree one goal
options.zh: 任务后尽快私下复盘：先听她自评，再给具体意见，一起定一个改进目标

options.en: Say nothing for now — she is new, and early criticism can easily destroy a student's confidence for good
options.zh: 暂时什么都不说——她还是新人，过早的批评很容易彻底摧毁一个学员的信心

options.en: Note the problem on her evaluation form and leave it for her preceptor to address later on
options.zh: 把问题写进她的评估表，留给带教老师日后处理

questions.explanationEn: Psychologically safe, timely feedback is private, prompt, specific, and two-way: her self-assessment first, concrete observations rather than global judgments, and one actionable goal. A is wrong because correcting her in front of the patient humiliates her and undermines the patient's confidence in the crew. C is wrong because silence denies her the learning she came for; well-delivered feedback builds confidence rather than destroying it. D is wrong because a form filled in later delays feedback past the point where it can change her next attempt and avoids the conversation altogether.
questions.explanationZh: 心理安全且及时的反馈应当是私下的、迅速的、具体的、双向的：先让她自评，给出具体观察而不是笼统评价，再约定一个可执行的目标。A 错：当着患者的面纠正她，既让她难堪，也削弱了患者对整个班组的信心。C 错：沉默剥夺了她来实习想学的东西；方式得当的反馈只会建立信心，而不是摧毁信心。D 错：事后填表会让反馈错过影响她下一次操作的时机，也回避了面对面的交流。

questions.questionEn: You are precepting a student. On a call for a seizing three-year-old, the student — who has never managed a pediatric airway — asks to take the lead. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正在带教一名学员。一趟三岁儿童抽搐的任务中，从未处理过儿科气道的学员请求主导这次处置。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Let her lead, since high-acuity calls are where students get their most valuable learning
options.zh: 让她来主导——毕竟危重任务恰恰是学员能学到最多实战经验的时候

options.en: Refuse without explanation and manage the call yourself, so there is no debate on scene
options.zh: 不作解释直接拒绝，自己处理这趟任务，免得在现场争论

options.en: Run the airway and key decisions yourself, give her defined support tasks, and debrief afterward
options.zh: 由你负责气道和关键决策，给她分派明确的辅助任务，事后再复盘

options.en: Let her lead while you talk her through each airway step in real time from beside her
options.zh: 让她主导，你在旁边实时口头指导每一个气道步骤

questions.explanationEn: Patient safety must be maintained whenever learners are involved — it is the boundary condition on all clinical teaching. A seizing child is not the place for a first pediatric airway; giving her real tasks matched to her level, plus a thorough debrief, preserves both the learning and the child. A is wrong because it gambles the child's airway on a first attempt. B is wrong because a flat refusal wastes a teaching opportunity and damages the relationship — a one-line “I'll lead this one, you take the suction and timing” works. D is wrong because real-time coaching still leaves an inexperienced learner in charge of a critical airway, and any hesitation costs time.
questions.explanationZh: 有学员参与时必须守住患者安全，这是所有临床教学的底线。抽搐的患儿不是学员第一次处理儿科气道的场合；给她与能力相匹配的真实任务，再做透彻的复盘，既保住了学习机会，也保住了孩子。A 错：这是拿孩子的气道去赌学员的第一次尝试。B 错：生硬拒绝浪费了教学机会，也伤害带教关系——一句“这次我来主导，你负责吸引和计时”就够了。D 错：即使实时指导，掌控危急气道的仍是一个没有经验的学员，她稍一犹豫就会耽误时间。

questions.questionEn: You have noticed over several months that one of your service's protocols consistently produces delays for a particular patient group, and newer published guidance recommends a different approach. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 几个月来你注意到，你所属服务机构的某项规程在某类患者身上持续造成延误，而较新发表的指南推荐了另一种做法。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Switch to the newer published guidance, since it reflects better and more current evidence
options.zh: 直接改为遵循较新发表的指南，因为它明显代表了更好、也更新的证据

options.en: Keep following the protocol and say nothing, since questioning protocols is not your role
options.zh: 继续照规程执行、什么也不说，因为质疑规程不是你的职责

options.en: Raise it informally with colleagues to see whether they agree before you decide anything
options.zh: 先私下和同事聊聊，看他们是否认同，再决定怎么办

options.en: Keep following the protocol while submitting cases and evidence to the guideline review process
options.zh: 继续执行现行规程，同时把具体病例和证据提交给负责审议指南的流程

questions.explanationEn: Giving feedback to the system when guidelines do not reflect best practice is an explicit competency — and it is done while continuing to follow the approved protocol, not by substituting your own. Structured, evidence-supported feedback is what actually changes a guideline. A is wrong because deviating on your own is practising outside your authorized protocols, however good the evidence looks. B is wrong because silent compliance lets a known problem continue for every future patient. C is wrong because informal agreement among colleagues is not a channel that can change anything.
