questions.explanationZh: 在指南未能反映最佳实践时向系统反馈，是一项明确的能力要求——而且要在继续执行既定规程的同时进行，而不是自行替换。有证据支撑的结构化反馈，才是真正能推动指南修订的途径。A 错：不管证据看起来多好，自行偏离都属于在授权规程之外执业。B 错：沉默服从会让已知问题在以后每一位患者身上继续存在。C 错：同事之间私下的共识不是能带来改变的渠道。

questions.questionEn: Your service sends you an individual dashboard showing your 12-lead ECG acquisition times are consistently in the slowest quartile of your station. What is the most constructive response?
questions.questionZh: 服务机构给你发来个人数据看板，显示你的 12 导联心电图采集时间长期处于本站最慢的四分之一区间。最有建设性的回应是什么？

options.en: Reflect on why, review your recent calls, learn from a colleague with fast times, and set a goal
options.zh: 反思原因，复盘近期任务，向采集快的同事请教，并定一个改进目标

options.en: Point out that your station covers the most complex calls, which explains the slower numbers
options.zh: 指出你们站承担的任务最复杂，所以数字偏慢情有可原

options.en: Disregard the dashboard, since acquisition time is a poor measure of the quality of care
options.zh: 不理会这份看板，因为采集时间并不能很好地衡量照护质量

options.en: Wait to see whether your supervisor raises it before deciding whether to take any action
options.zh: 先等主管会不会提起，再决定要不要采取行动

questions.explanationEn: Identifying opportunities to improve by reflecting on your own performance using internal and external data is exactly what a dashboard is for; self-review, peer learning, and a concrete goal turn the data into practice change. B is wrong because you are in the slowest quartile of your own station — your colleagues face the same call mix. C is wrong because time to a 12-lead affects how quickly a STEMI is recognized, so dismissing the metric dismisses something that matters to patients. D is wrong because waiting to be told treats the data as a threat rather than a learning source.
questions.explanationZh: 利用内部和外部数据反思自身表现、发现改进机会，正是绩效看板存在的意义；自我复盘、向同事学习、设定具体目标，才能把数据转化为实践上的改进。B 错：你是在本站内排在最慢的四分之一，同站同事面对的是同样的任务构成。C 错：12 导联心电图采集的快慢直接影响 STEMI 被识别的速度，否定这个指标就是否定一件关系到患者的事。D 错：坐等别人指出，是把数据当成威胁而不是学习来源。

questions.questionEn: You have been asked to lead a case review at your station about a call that went badly. What approach will make the session most useful?
questions.questionZh: 你被要求在站里主持一次病例复盘，讨论一趟处理得不好的任务。什么方式能让这次复盘最有价值？

options.en: Present a step-by-step account of what the crew should have done differently on the call
options.zh: 逐步讲解该班组当时本应如何处置

options.en: Keep the discussion general and avoid the specific call, so no one feels singled out
options.zh: 讨论保持泛泛而谈，避开这趟具体任务，免得有人觉得被针对

options.en: Set blame-free ground rules, rebuild the case with what was known at the time, and agree on changes
options.zh: 先定下不追责的规则，按当时掌握的信息还原病例，最后商定改进措施

options.en: Invite the crew involved to explain their reasoning to the whole group and then answer everyone's questions
options.zh: 请当事班组向全体同事解释他们当时的判断思路，再逐一回答大家的提问

questions.explanationEn: Leading a learning activity well needs psychological safety plus rigour: explicit blame-free ground rules, reconstruction of the case using only what was known at the time (which guards against hindsight bias), group analysis of what shaped the decisions, and concrete agreed changes. A is wrong because lecturing the “right answers” wastes the group's insight and invites hindsight bias. B is wrong because avoiding the actual case removes the learning the session exists for. D is wrong because putting the involved crew on the spot to justify themselves breeds defensiveness rather than reflection.
questions.explanationZh: 主持好一次学习活动，需要心理安全与严谨并重：明确的不追责规则，只用当时掌握的信息还原病例（避免事后诸葛亮），集体分析是什么影响了当时的决定，最后形成具体的改进共识。A 错：单向讲授“正确答案”浪费了集体智慧，也容易陷入事后诸葛亮。B 错：避开具体病例，这次复盘就失去了存在的意义。D 错：让当事班组当众自证，只会激起防御心理而不是反思。

questions.questionEn: Three weeks after a pediatric drowning call, you are sleeping four hours a night, snapping at your family, and you feel your chest tighten every time you drive past that lake. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一次儿童溺水任务过去三周后，你每晚只睡四小时、对家人动辄发火，每次开车经过那个湖时都感到胸口发紧。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Treat these as warning signs and reach out now — to peer support, your EFAP, or a clinician
options.zh: 把这些视为警示信号，马上求助：同伴支持、EFAP 或专业心理人员

options.en: Give it more time, since most reactions to a hard call settle on their own within a few months
options.zh: 再等等看——大多数人对艰难任务的反应，几个月之内都会自己慢慢平复

options.en: Ask to be kept off pediatric calls until the symptoms ease, so you are not reminded of it
options.zh: 申请暂时不派儿科任务，直到症状缓解，免得再想起那件事

options.en: Step up your exercise and sleep routine on your own, and reassess how you feel in a month
options.zh: 自己加强运动、调整作息，一个月后再看看感觉如何

questions.explanationEn: Poor sleep, irritability, and a physical reaction to reminders of the event three weeks later are warning signs of a stress injury, and the competency is to recognize and act on them — tell someone and get help early, which works far better than waiting. B is wrong because symptoms that are still disrupting sleep and family life at three weeks tend to entrench if you wait. C is wrong because avoidance usually strengthens a trauma response rather than resolving it. D is wrong because exercise and sleep help, but self-care alone is not enough for symptoms at this level, and another month's delay postpones real help.
questions.explanationZh: 三周后仍然睡不好、易怒，一碰到与事件相关的东西身体就有反应，这些是应激损伤的警示信号，而这项能力要求你识别并采取行动——告诉别人、尽早求助，效果远好于观望。B 错：已经三周还在影响睡眠和家庭生活的症状，越等越容易固化。C 错：回避通常会强化而不是化解创伤反应。D 错：运动和睡眠有帮助，但这种程度的症状单靠自我调理不够，再拖一个月只会推迟真正的帮助。

questions.questionEn: A normally meticulous colleague has been arriving late, missing documentation, and eating lunch alone in his car for the past month. Today he told a patient's family to "just calm down" — completely out of character. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一位平时一丝不苟的同事，这一个月来经常迟到、文书遗漏、独自在车里吃午饭。今天他对一位患者家属说"你冷静点行不行"——完全不像他平时的样子。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Report his comment to the family to your supervisor, and leave the rest for management
options.zh: 把他对家属说话的事报告主管，剩下的交给管理层处理

options.en: Speak with him privately and without judgment: name what you've noticed and ask how he's really doing
options.zh: 私下、不带评判地找他谈：说出你注意到的变化，问问他真实的状态

options.en: Say nothing for now, since everyone has rough patches and his private life is really none of your business
options.zh: 先什么都不说——谁都有不顺的时候，他的私事也轮不到你管

options.en: Check with other colleagues whether they've noticed the same changes before you say anything
options.zh: 先问问其他同事有没有注意到同样的变化，再决定要不要跟他说

questions.explanationEn: Withdrawal, slipping performance, and uncharacteristic irritability are classic warning signs that a colleague is struggling; learning to spot stress in colleagues matters because early recognition can stop things getting worse. A private, caring conversation opens the door without cornering him. A is wrong because reporting only the incident treats a symptom as misconduct and misses the person behind it. C is wrong because silence leaves a colleague to deteriorate alone. D is wrong because canvassing others first turns concern into gossip and can destroy the trust he would need to accept help.
questions.explanationZh: 退缩、表现下滑、反常的易怒，是同事状态出问题的典型警示信号；要学会在同事身上发现应激征象，因为及早发现能防止情况恶化。一次私下的、关切的谈话能打开话题，又不让他难堪。A 错：只上报那次冲突，等于把症状当成违纪处理，忽略了背后的人。C 错：沉默会让同事独自一步步恶化。D 错：先去问别人，关心就变成了议论，还可能毁掉他接受帮助所需要的信任。

questions.questionEn: You are at hour 14 of a 16-hour shift with no meal break. You just caught yourself drawing up the wrong concentration of a medication, and a moment ago you drifted across the centre line while driving. Dispatch is holding two calls. What must you do?
questions.questionZh: 你已经连续工作到 16 小时班次的第 14 小时，中间没有用餐休息。你刚刚发现自己抽错了药物浓度，而就在片刻前开车时车身压过了中线。调度还压着两趟任务待派。你必须怎么做？

options.en: Take the calls, but have your partner drive and double-check every medication you prepare
options.zh: 接下任务，但让搭档开车，并让他复核你准备的每一种药

options.en: Push through the last two hours, since calls are holding and the public needs ambulance coverage
options.zh: 撑完最后两小时——任务在排队，公众需要有救护车随时保障

options.en: Tell your supervisor now that you are unsafe to continue, ask for relief, and take no more calls
options.zh: 立即告诉主管你已无法安全继续工作，申请换人，不再接任务

options.en: Take only low-acuity calls for the rest of the shift, so the risk of an error stays small
options.zh: 本班剩余时间只接轻症任务，把出错风险降到最低

questions.explanationEn: A drawing-up error and a lane departure are not early warnings — they are impairment that is already producing near misses. The competency is explicit: remove yourself from practice when you cannot perform safely; a paramedic who has been working for many hours without rest cannot safely drive an ambulance or give medications. A is wrong because a partner's checks cannot restore your judgment, and you would still be making decisions on scene. B is wrong because pushing through while impaired is exactly how fatigue harms patients and crews. D is wrong because low-acuity calls still involve driving and medications, and a call's acuity can change after you arrive.
questions.explanationZh: 抽错药、开车压线，不是能力受损的早期预警——它们本身就是能力受损，而且已经造成了险情。这项能力的要求很明确：无法安全执业时，要主动退出执业；连续工作多个小时、没有休息的救护员，无法安全地驾驶救护车或给药。A 错：搭档复核无法恢复你的判断力，而且到了现场还是你在做决定。B 错：在能力受损时硬撑，正是疲劳伤害患者和同事的典型方式。D 错：轻症任务同样要开车、要用药，而且到了现场病情也可能变化。

questions.questionEn: After a difficult call, your partner says quietly: "I don't know, man. Some days I wonder if I'm even cut out for this anymore." What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一趟艰难的任务后，搭档低声说："我也说不好。有时候我怀疑自己是不是根本不适合干这行了。"最佳回应是什么？

options.en: Reassure him quickly — “Don't be silly, you're one of the best medics here” — to lift his mood
options.zh: 赶紧安慰他——“别瞎想，你可是这儿最好的救护员之一”——让他马上振作起来

options.en: Suggest he take a few days off, then steer the talk to something lighter to cheer him up
options.zh: 建议他休几天假，然后把话题转到轻松的事上，让他开心点

options.en: Stay with it — “That sounds heavy. What's been going on?” — listen, then ask who he talks to
options.zh: 顺着说下去——“听起来挺沉重，最近怎么了？”——认真听，再问他平时找谁倾诉

options.en: Tell him about a call that shook you badly, so he knows he is not alone in feeling this way
options.zh: 跟他讲一趟曾让你深受打击的任务，让他知道有这种感受的不止他一个

questions.explanationEn: Offering non-judgmental help to a colleague means opening the conversation rather than closing it: an open question, genuine listening, and a gentle check on whether he has support. A is wrong because rushed reassurance signals that the topic is unwelcome. B is wrong because changing the subject shuts a door he took courage to open; time off may help later, but it is not a response to what he just said. D is wrong because turning to your own story moves the focus off him at the very moment he opened up.
questions.explanationZh: 向同事提供不带评判的帮助，意味着把话题打开而不是关上：一个开放式提问、真诚的倾听，再温和地确认他有没有可以倾诉的人。A 错：急着安慰传达的信号是“这个话题我不想听”。B 错：转移话题等于关上了他鼓起勇气才打开的门；休假以后也许有用，但不是对他这句话的回应。D 错：转而讲自己的经历，会在他刚刚开口的那一刻把焦点从他身上移开。

questions.questionEn: You are starting your first year as a paramedic. What is the most effective approach to building support systems for a long career?
questions.questionZh: 你刚开始救护职业生涯的第一年。为长期从业建立支持体系，最有效的做法是什么？

options.en: Build supports now while you're well: know your peer team and EFAP, and keep friends outside EMS
options.zh: 趁状态好就建立支持：熟悉同伴支持和 EFAP，保持 EMS 圈外的友谊

options.en: Wait until you have had a difficult call, so you know what kind of support you actually need
options.zh: 等真正经历过一趟艰难的任务再说，到那时你才知道自己究竟需要哪种支持

options.en: Rely mainly on your crew, since only other paramedics truly understand what the work is like
options.zh: 主要依靠班组同事，因为只有同行才真正理解这份工作

options.en: Focus on physical fitness first, and look into mental health supports only if problems ever appear
options.zh: 先专注体能训练，等真出了问题再去了解心理支持

questions.explanationEn: The time to guard against burnout is at the very start of your career: supports built while you are well are the ones you actually use in a crisis, because you already know who to call. Keeping relationships and activities with people outside EMS, and having someone to talk to, are core protections. B is wrong because waiting for a bad call means building a network when you are already depleted. C is wrong because socializing only within EMS narrows your perspective; time with people outside the job is specifically recommended. D is wrong because physical health matters, but treating mental health as a contingency plan reverses the logic of prevention.
questions.explanationZh: 预防职业倦怠要从入行第一天开始：状态好时建立起来的支持，才是危机中真正用得上的，因为你早就知道该找谁。和 EMS 圈外的人保持来往和共同活动、有人可以倾诉，是最基本的保护。B 错：等出了事再建，等于在最耗竭的时候搭建人脉。C 错：只在同行圈子里来往会让视野变窄，教材特别建议多和圈外的人相处。D 错：身体健康固然重要，但把心理健康当成“出事再说”的备用方案，完全颠倒了预防的逻辑。

questions.questionEn: You work in a community hit hard by the toxic drug crisis and have responded to the same few blocks for repeated overdoses, including two people you had revived before who later died. You notice yourself becoming numb and cynical toward these patients. What is the best understanding and response?
questions.questionZh: 你所在的社区受有毒药物危机冲击严重，你反复在同样的几个街区处置过量用药，其中两名你曾救回的人后来还是去世了。你发现自己对这些患者开始变得麻木、愤世嫉俗。最恰当的理解和应对是什么？

options.en: This is normal professional adaptation to a caseload that EMS cannot fix, and needs no action
options.zh: 这是面对 EMS 根本无力解决的任务类型时正常的职业适应，不需要做什么

options.en: This reflects the patients' own repeated choices, so your frustration is a reasonable reaction
options.zh: 这反映的是患者自己一再的选择，你的挫败感是合理的反应

options.en: Numbness and cynicism are warning signs of burnout; talk to peer or professional support and debrief
options.zh: 麻木和愤世嫉俗是职业倦怠的警示信号；应找同伴或专业支持倾诉，并做复盘

options.en: Request a transfer to a station with a different call profile, so the exposure simply stops
options.zh: 申请调到任务类型不同的站点，让这种暴露就此停止

questions.explanationEn: Burnout is a consequence of chronic, unrelieved stress, and cynical, negative attitudes are among its warning signs — signals to stop, reflect, and get support: talk with someone, use peer or professional support, and debrief tough calls. The realities of the community you serve can drive this, and unchecked cynicism also threatens the care of patients who are already stigmatized. A is wrong because calling it normal adaptation ignores a recognized warning sign. B is wrong because blaming patients deepens the cynicism and shows it is already affecting your attitude to care. D is wrong because a transfer may sometimes be reasonable, but it does not deal with the stress you are already carrying.
questions.explanationZh: 职业倦怠是长期得不到缓解的压力造成的，而愤世嫉俗、消极的态度正是它的警示信号之一——提醒你停下来反思、寻求支持：找人倾诉，利用同伴或专业支持，艰难任务后做复盘。你所服务社区的现实处境可能引发这种状态，而任其发展的愤世嫉俗，也会威胁到本已被污名化的患者所得到的照护。A 错：把它说成正常适应，等于无视一个公认的警示信号。B 错：归咎于患者只会加深愤世嫉俗，也说明它已经在影响你对照护的态度。D 错：调岗有时或许合理，但解决不了你身上已经积累的压力。

questions.questionEn: Which change in a colleague should most urgently prompt you to act on concerns about their well-being?
questions.questionZh: 同事出现哪种变化时，最需要你紧急就其身心状态采取行动？

options.en: Comments suggesting hopelessness, or that colleagues would be better off without them
options.zh: 说出流露绝望的话，或表示同事们没有他会过得更好

options.en: Becoming noticeably quieter and less social around the station over the past few weeks
options.zh: 最近几周在站里明显变得沉默、不太和人来往

options.en: Making more dark jokes after difficult calls than they used to, sometimes in front of others
options.zh: 艰难任务后比以前更多地开黑色玩笑，有时还当着别人的面

options.en: Taking more sick days than usual over the past two months, often right after night shifts
options.zh: 过去两个月病假比平时多，而且常在夜班之后请假

questions.explanationEn: Statements of hopelessness or of others being better off without them suggest suicidal thinking, and every such statement must be taken seriously. Respond immediately: ask directly about suicidal thoughts — asking does not plant the idea — stay with the person, and connect them with crisis support. B is wrong as the most urgent choice because withdrawal is a real warning sign of stress worth acting on, but it does not signal immediate danger. C is wrong because more dark humour is a concern to follow up, not a sign of imminent risk. D is wrong because rising absence deserves a caring conversation, but it lacks the urgency of language suggesting the person may be thinking of ending their life.
questions.explanationZh: 流露绝望、或说“没有我别人会更好”，提示可能有自杀念头，而任何这类言语都必须认真对待。应立即回应：直接询问对方是否有自杀的想法——问出来并不会让人产生这个念头——陪着对方，并帮他联系危机支持。B 错：退缩是值得关注的应激信号，但并不提示迫在眉睫的危险，不是最紧急的。C 错：黑色玩笑增多需要跟进关心，但不代表即将发生危险。D 错：病假增多值得关切地谈一谈，但紧迫性远不及“可能想结束生命”的言语。

questions.questionEn: You attend an Indigenous man with abdominal pain. In the ED, you overhear your partner tell the triage nurse: "Probably just drinking again — you know how it is with these guys." Your patient has no signs of intoxication. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你出勤处置一名腹痛的原住民男性。在急诊，你听到搭档对分诊护士说："多半又是喝多了——这些人你懂的。"而你的患者并无任何醉酒表现。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Say nothing at the hospital, but raise the comment privately with your partner afterward
options.zh: 在医院不作声，事后再私下和搭档谈这句话

options.en: Tell the nurse now there are no signs of intoxication and give your findings, then address and report it
options.zh: 立即告诉护士患者毫无醉酒表现并说明评估发现，随后与搭档沟通并上报

options.en: Make sure your own written report is accurate and complete, and let it speak for itself rather than argue
options.zh: 确保你自己的书面报告准确完整，让文书本身去说明一切，不必在当场和人争论

options.en: Ask the nurse quietly to disregard your partner's comment, without explaining anything further
options.zh: 悄悄请护士别理会搭档那句话，不再多作解释

questions.explanationEn: An unfounded intoxication label on an Indigenous patient can lower triage priority, delay investigation, and lead to a serious cause of abdominal pain being missed. Working toward reconciliation means identifying and addressing Indigenous-specific racism when it happens: correcting the clinical picture immediately protects this patient, and addressing it with your partner and reporting it through your service's process deals with the pattern. A is wrong because the false label keeps shaping this patient's care while you wait. C is wrong because the nurse is triaging now from what she heard, and the written report may not be read before decisions are made. D is wrong because an unexplained aside does not replace the false information with the actual findings, and leaves the behaviour unaddressed.
questions.explanationZh: 给原住民患者贴上毫无根据的“醉酒”标签，可能降低分诊等级、延误检查，导致腹痛的严重病因被漏诊。推进和解，意味着在原住民特定的种族歧视发生时及时识别和处理：立即纠正临床信息保护的是眼前这位患者，随后与搭档沟通并按机构流程上报，处理的是这种模式本身。A 错：在你等待的时候，这个错误标签一直在影响患者的照护。C 错：护士此刻就在根据她听到的话分诊，书面报告未必能在决策之前被看到。D 错：一句不加解释的私下提醒，并没有用真实的评估发现取代错误信息，搭档的行为也没有得到处理。

questions.questionEn: Which action best reflects a trauma-informed approach when assessing a patient who appears highly guarded and reluctant to be touched?
questions.questionZh: 在评估一位显得高度戒备、抗拒被触碰的患者时，哪种做法最能体现创伤知情（trauma-informed）的照护方式？

options.en: Ask her gently what happened to her in the past, so you can understand her reaction to care
options.zh: 温和地问她过去经历过什么，以便理解她为什么会对照护有这样的反应

options.en: Complete the assessment as quickly as possible, to keep the time she feels distressed short
options.zh: 尽快完成评估，把她感到不适的时间缩到最短

options.en: Explain each step first, ask before touching, offer choices, and let her stop at any time
options.zh: 每一步先说明，触碰前先征得同意，给她选择，并允许她随时叫停

options.en: Have a paramedic of the same gender do the assessment instead, then proceed with the usual exam
options.zh: 改由同性别的救护员来评估，然后照常检查

questions.explanationEn: Trauma-informed care rests on safety, choice, and control — restoring the sense of agency that trauma takes away. Explaining before acting, asking permission, offering options, and honouring her right to stop achieve this whatever her history is. A is wrong because probing for the traumatic event risks re-traumatizing her and is not needed to care for her. B is wrong because rushing takes away the very control she needs. D is wrong because a same-gender provider can be offered as a choice, but swapping without asking and then carrying on as usual misses the core principle.
questions.explanationZh: 创伤知情照护建立在安全感、选择权和掌控感之上——也就是恢复被创伤夺走的自主感。先说明再动手、征得同意、提供选择、尊重她随时叫停的权利，无论她有怎样的经历都适用。A 错：追问创伤经历有再次伤害她的风险，而且照护她并不需要知道这些。B 错：匆忙操作恰恰剥夺了她最需要的掌控感。D 错：同性别的救护员可以作为一个选项提供给她，但不问她的意见就换人、然后照常检查，没有抓住核心原则。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old woman calls 911 for the third time in six weeks after falls. Her home has loose rugs, no grab bars, poor lighting, and she tells you her son visits only monthly. She is uninjured today and refuses transport. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一位 82 岁的女性六周内第三次因跌倒拨打 911。她家里地毯松脱、没有扶手、照明昏暗，她说儿子每月才来一次。她今天没有受伤，并拒绝转运。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Document the refusal and advise her to see her family doctor about the falls when she can
options.zh: 记录她拒绝转运，并建议她有空时就跌倒问题去看家庭医生

options.en: Explain that she will keep falling and getting hurt unless she agrees to move into an assisted-living facility
options.zh: 告诉她除非同意搬进辅助生活机构，否则还会继续摔倒

options.en: With her consent, fix the hazards you can, and refer her to falls-prevention or community services
options.zh: 征得她同意后，处理力所能及的隐患，并把她转介给防跌倒或社区服务

options.en: Phone her son and tell him he needs to visit more often, since she clearly needs more help
options.zh: 打电话给她儿子，告诉他需要多来看望，因为她显然需要更多帮助

questions.explanationEn: Working with patients on the determinants affecting their health — here, environmental hazards such as loose rugs and poor lighting, which are common causes of falls in older adults, plus thin social support — means acting on the causes, not just the latest fall. Removing hazards you can see and referring her into community falls-prevention, home health, or community paramedicine services, then documenting the hazards and the referral, addresses the risk of a fourth call. A is wrong because documenting a refusal changes nothing about why she keeps falling. B is wrong because pressuring her toward assisted living overrides her autonomy when other options exist. D is wrong because contacting her son without her consent goes around her and discloses her health information.
questions.explanationZh: 与患者一同应对影响其健康的因素——这里是松脱的地毯、昏暗的照明等环境隐患（老年人跌倒的常见外因），以及薄弱的社会支持——意味着处理根源，而不只是处理这一次跌倒。当场清除看得见的隐患，再把她转介给社区防跌倒、居家健康或社区辅助医疗服务，并记录隐患和转介情况，才能应对第四次呼救的风险。A 错：只记录拒绝转运，改变不了她反复跌倒的原因。B 错：明明还有别的办法，却施压让她搬去辅助生活机构，侵犯了她的自主权。D 错：未经她同意就联系儿子，既绕开了她本人，也泄露了她的健康信息。

questions.questionEn: Reviewing your own practice, you realize you tend to ask fewer questions and spend less time on scene with patients who are visibly homeless. What does professional self-awareness require of you?
questions.questionZh: 复盘自己的执业时，你意识到面对明显无家可归的患者，自己往往问得更少、在现场停留的时间也更短。职业自我觉察要求你怎么做？

options.en: Acknowledge it as a bias, examine where it comes from, and apply the same assessment standard to all
options.zh: 承认这是一种偏见，反思它从何而来，并对所有患者采用同样的评估标准

options.en: Accept it as a realistic adaptation, since these patients often decline a detailed assessment
options.zh: 把它当成一种务实的调整，反正这类患者本来就常常不愿意接受详细的评估

options.en: Conclude that the pattern reflects genuine differences in how serious these calls tend to be
options.zh: 认定这种模式反映的是这类任务在严重程度上的真实差异

options.en: Ask your partner to lead assessments with these patients from now on, to keep care consistent
options.zh: 今后让搭档主导对这类患者的评估，以保持照护一致

questions.explanationEn: Practising self-awareness to minimize personal and cognitive bias means naming the bias, understanding where it comes from, and correcting your behaviour with one consistent standard — then monitoring yourself over time. B is wrong because assuming these patients will decline is part of the bias; it is the reason for asking less, not a justification. C is wrong because people experiencing homelessness carry a higher, not lower, burden of undetected illness, so a shorter assessment is exactly how serious conditions get missed. D is wrong because handing these patients to your partner outsources a problem that is yours to fix and leaves your own practice unchanged.
questions.explanationZh: 以自我觉察来减少个人偏见和认知偏差，意味着直面这种偏见、弄清它的来源，用统一的标准纠正自己的行为，并持续自我监测。B 错：认定这类患者会拒绝，本身就是偏见的一部分——它是你问得少的原因，而不是理由。C 错：无家可归者未被发现的疾病负担更高而不是更低，评估缩水恰恰是漏诊严重疾病的方式。D 错：把这类患者交给搭档，是把本该由你自己解决的问题外包出去，你自己的做法一点没变。

questions.questionEn: A patient with a serious infection tells you she has been treating it with traditional medicines from her community and wants to continue alongside hospital care. How should you respond?
questions.questionZh: 一位患有严重感染的患者告诉你，她一直在用本社区的传统药物治疗，并希望在接受医院治疗的同时继续使用。你应该如何回应？

options.en: Explain that traditional remedies are unproven, and advise her to stop them during treatment
options.zh: 解释传统疗法未经证实，建议她治疗期间停用

options.en: Say nothing about it, since it is not relevant to the prehospital care you are providing
options.zh: 不予置评，因为这与你提供的院前处置无关

options.en: Ask respectfully what she uses and when, record it, pass it on at handover, and support her wish
options.zh: 尊重地询问她用了什么、何时用的，做好记录，交接时转达，并支持她的意愿

options.en: Advise her to keep the traditional treatments to herself, so the hospital staff take her symptoms seriously
options.zh: 建议她别向医院提起自己在用传统疗法，免得医护人员不把她的症状当回事

questions.explanationEn: Showing respect and humility, and bringing the patient's own understanding of health and healing into her care, means treating traditional medicine as legitimate context — clinically relevant because substances may interact, and culturally important to her. Her hospital team can then plan with her how to combine the two. A is wrong because dismissing it damages trust and often just drives the practice out of sight. B is wrong because ignoring it loses real clinical information. D is wrong because advising concealment actively teaches her to hide information from the team caring for her.
questions.explanationZh: 展现尊重与谦逊、把患者自己对健康与疗愈的理解纳入照护，意味着把传统医药当作正当的背景信息——它有临床意义（成分可能存在相互作用），对她也有文化上的重要性。这样医院团队才能和她一起商量如何结合两种疗法。A 错：轻视传统医药会损害信任，往往只会让她转为偷偷使用。B 错：不闻不问会丢掉真实的临床信息。D 错：建议她隐瞒，等于主动教她向照护团队隐藏信息。

questions.questionEn: An Elder from a remote community requires transport to a regional hospital four hours away. She is anxious about going alone — she has no family in that city and speaks limited English. What is the best action?
questions.questionZh: 一位来自偏远社区的长者需要转运到四小时车程外的地区医院。她对独自前往感到焦虑——她在那座城市没有家人，英语能力也有限。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Reassure her warmly that the hospital staff will take good care of her once she gets there
options.zh: 温和地安慰她，到了医院工作人员自然会好好照顾她

options.en: Explain that ambulances cannot take passengers, so she will need to arrange her own support
options.zh: 说明救护车不能搭载随行人员，她需要自己安排支持

options.en: Ask whether a support person can come, and alert the hospital to her language and support needs
options.zh: 问问能否有一位支持者陪同，并提前告知医院她的语言和支持需求

options.en: Suggest she decline the transfer and look for care closer to home, where she has family
options.zh: 建议她拒绝转院，改在离家近、有家人的地方就医

questions.explanationEn: Adjusting care to promote equitable outcomes means actively removing the barriers she faces — isolation, language, and distance from her community. Asking about an escort, notifying the receiving hospital so interpretation and an Indigenous patient navigator can be arranged, and passing her concerns on at handover turn a foreseeable bad experience into accessible care. A is wrong because general reassurance removes none of these barriers. B is wrong because it states a blanket rule without checking your service's escort policy. D is wrong because steering her away from care she needs makes the very inequity worse.
questions.explanationZh: 调整照护以促进公平结局，意味着主动清除她面临的障碍——孤立无援、语言不通、远离自己的社区。询问能否有人陪同，提前通知接收医院以便安排翻译和原住民患者协导员，并在交接时转达她的顾虑，能把一次可以预见的糟糕经历变成可及的照护。A 错：泛泛的安慰解决不了任何一个障碍。B 错：没有查机构的随行政策就断言不能陪同。D 错：劝她放弃所需的治疗，只会加剧本来就存在的不公平。

questions.questionEn: Your patient's chart lists a name and sex marker that do not match how the patient introduces themselves. They give you a different name and use they/them pronouns. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 患者病历上的姓名和性别标记与其自我介绍不符。对方告诉你另一个名字，并使用 they/them 代词。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Use the name and pronouns they give, record it alongside the legal name, and use it at handover
options.zh: 使用患者告知的姓名和代词，同时记下法定姓名，交接时也这样称呼

options.en: Use the legal name on the chart throughout, so the medical record stays clear, consistent, and accurate
options.zh: 全程使用病历上的法定姓名，这样医疗记录才能保持清晰、一致和准确

options.en: Avoid using any name or pronouns at all during the call, so that you stay completely neutral
options.zh: 整个出勤过程中完全不用任何姓名或代词，保持绝对中立

options.en: Record only the name the patient gives you, and leave the legal name out of your report
options.zh: 报告里只写患者告知的姓名，不写法定姓名

questions.explanationEn: Contributing to culturally safe care for equity-deserving groups means using the patient's name and pronouns as a baseline of respect, while documenting both identifiers so records, medications, and results link correctly. B is wrong because defaulting to the legal name is a well-known source of distress and disengagement from care, and it is unnecessary when both names are recorded. C is wrong because avoiding names altogether is awkward, still othering, and can cause identification errors. D is wrong because leaving out the legal name risks mismatched records, results, and medications in the health system.
questions.explanationZh: 为应受公平对待的群体营造文化安全的照护，意味着把使用患者自己的姓名和代词作为基本尊重，同时记录两个身份标识，确保病历、用药和检验结果能正确对应。B 错：一律用法定姓名是众所周知会让患者痛苦、疏远医疗的做法，而且两个名字都记录下来就不存在混乱问题。C 错：完全回避称呼既别扭，仍然让人感到被区别对待，还可能造成身份识别错误。D 错：不写法定姓名，可能在医疗系统里造成病历、检验结果和用药的错配。

questions.questionEn: You respond to a non-fatal opioid overdose. After naloxone the patient is alert and oriented. You explain that the naloxone may wear off before the opioid does and urge him to come to hospital, but he has capacity and still refuses. What is the most valuable harm-reduction step before you leave?
questions.questionZh: 你出勤处置一起非致死性阿片类药物过量。使用纳洛酮（naloxone）后，患者神志清楚、定向力正常。你向他解释纳洛酮的作用可能比阿片类药物先消退，并劝他去医院，但他具备决定能力，仍然拒绝。离开前最有价值的减低伤害措施是什么？

options.en: Warn him clearly that the next overdose could kill him, so fear will motivate him to stop using
options.zh: 明确警告他下一次过量可能会要命，让恐惧促使他戒掉

options.en: Arrange for someone to stay with him, point him to a free naloxone kit, and advise never using alone
options.zh: 安排有人陪着他，告诉他去哪里免费领纳洛酮急救包，并劝他绝不要独自用药

options.en: Spend the remaining time persuading him to enter a treatment program before you clear the scene
options.zh: 把剩下的时间都用来劝他参加戒治项目，然后再撤离

options.en: Document the refusal thoroughly and clear the scene, since he has now made an informed choice
options.zh: 把拒绝过程详细记录下来就撤离，毕竟他已经在充分知情的情况下作出了选择

questions.explanationEn: Naloxone has a shorter half-life than many opioids, so a patient can slip back into respiratory depression after it wears off; that is why patients should generally not be left after naloxone, and why you first urge transport. When a capable adult still refuses, health promotion means reducing his risk of dying in the next hours: someone with him who can call 911 and give naloxone, a free take-home naloxone kit, never using alone, and clear advice to call back. A is wrong because fear-based warnings rarely change behaviour. C is wrong because pressing treatment on someone not seeking it usually ends the conversation, and it does nothing about tonight's risk. D is wrong because documentation alone leaves him no safer if he re-sedates alone.
questions.explanationZh: 纳洛酮（naloxone）的半衰期比许多阿片类药物短，药效消退后患者可能再次出现呼吸抑制；所以原则上用过纳洛酮的患者不应留在现场，你也应先劝他转运。如果有决定能力的成年人仍然拒绝，健康促进就是降低他接下来几小时内的死亡风险：有人陪着他、能打 911 并给纳洛酮，告诉他去哪里免费领纳洛酮急救包，劝他绝不要独自用药，并明确告诉他需要时再呼叫。A 错：恐吓式警告很少能改变行为。C 错：向没有意愿的人硬推戒治往往会终结对话，而且对今晚的风险毫无帮助。D 错：只做记录，他一旦独自再次昏迷，并不会比你来之前更安全。

questions.questionEn: At your station, a senior paramedic regularly refers to patients from a particular neighbourhood as "the usual garbage from down there." Newer staff have started using the phrase too. What is the most effective response?
questions.questionZh: 在你所在的站点，一位资深救护员经常把某个街区来的患者称作"那边惯常的垃圾"。新入职的员工也开始跟着这么说了。最有效的应对是什么？

options.en: Refuse to use the phrase yourself, and hope the newer staff gradually follow your quiet example
options.zh: 自己坚决不用这种说法，希望新员工慢慢以你为榜样

options.en: Call it out calmly each time — “we don't talk about patients that way” — and escalate if it persists
options.zh: 每次听到都平静地指出——“我们不这样说患者”——情况持续就向上反映

options.en: Report the senior paramedic to the regulator for unprofessional conduct, so the behaviour stops for good
options.zh: 以不专业行为向监管机构举报这位资深救护员，让这种行为停止

options.en: Avoid working shifts with that paramedic where possible, so you are not part of the culture
options.zh: 尽量避免和他同班，免得自己成为这种文化的一部分

questions.explanationEn: Challenging biases that marginalize a community requires visible action, because silence is read as agreement — which is exactly how the phrase spread to newer staff. Naming it calmly in the moment, without attacking the person, resets the norm and gives juniors permission to object too; raising an entrenched pattern with leadership addresses the culture. A is wrong because quiet modelling is not enough to counter a norm that is actively spreading. C is wrong because going straight to the regulator skips every reasonable step, from a direct word to raising it with leadership. D is wrong because avoidance leaves the newer staff with only one example to follow and the norm unchallenged.
questions.explanationZh: 挑战那些边缘化某个社区的偏见，需要看得见的行动，因为沉默会被当成默许——新员工正是这样跟着学的。当场平和地、不针对个人地指出来，能够重置规范，也让资历浅的同事有底气表达异议；对已经固化的模式，向管理层反映才能处理文化层面的问题。A 错：仅靠默默以身作则，抵挡不了一个正在扩散的群体规范。C 错：直接举报到监管机构，跳过了从当面提醒到向管理层反映的所有合理步骤。D 错：一味回避，新员工就只剩一个榜样可学，这种风气也无人挑战。

questions.questionEn: A mother with two young children calls for her child's asthma exacerbation. During the call you notice the apartment is cold, visibly mouldy, and she mentions the landlord has ignored repair requests for months. What is the most appropriate advocacy action?
questions.questionZh: 一位带着两个幼儿的母亲因孩子哮喘发作呼救。出勤中你注意到公寓寒冷、有明显霉斑，她还提到房东几个月来对维修请求置之不理。最恰当的倡导行动是什么？

options.en: Advise her to move to better housing as soon as she can, for the sake of the children's health
options.zh: 为了孩子的健康，建议她尽快搬到更好的住处

options.en: Treat the child, document the housing conditions, and with her consent connect her to supports
options.zh: 处理孩子的发作，记录居住条件，并在她同意后为她对接支持服务

options.en: Contact the landlord yourself on her behalf to demand that the mould and heating be repaired
options.zh: 你亲自代她联系房东，要求修好霉菌和供暖问题

options.en: Report the housing conditions to child protection services as a safety concern for the children
options.zh: 以孩子的安全受到威胁为由，向儿童保护机构举报这家人的居住条件

questions.explanationEn: Advocating with families to reduce environmental determinants of health means connecting them to the people with the authority you lack: your documentation carries the finding forward to the hospital team, and consented referrals — an ED social worker, tenant advocacy, or public health — can push for action on mould and heating. A is wrong because it ignores why she has not moved: cost and the lack of alternatives. C is wrong because contacting the landlord yourself is outside your role and could expose her to retaliation. D is wrong because landlord neglect is not parental neglect; a child-protection report here would punish a mother for poverty (signs of actual neglect or abuse would be a different matter).
questions.explanationZh: 与家庭一起倡导、减少环境方面的健康决定因素，意味着把他们对接给拥有你所没有的权限的人：你的记录会把这一发现带给医院团队，而经她同意的转介——急诊社工、租客权益服务或公共卫生部门——才能推动霉菌和供暖问题的解决。A 错：这忽略了她为什么一直没搬——房租负担和没有别的选择。C 错：亲自去找房东超出了你的职责，还可能让她遭到报复。D 错：房东失职不等于父母疏忽，在这种情况下举报儿童保护，等于因为贫穷而惩罚一位母亲（如果确有疏忽或虐待迹象则另当别论）。

questions.questionEn: A woman with visible injuries is evasive about how they occurred, and her partner stays close and answers for her. Applying a trauma-informed approach, what should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一位身上有明显外伤的女性对受伤经过含糊其辞，她的伴侣一直紧挨着她并替她回答。基于创伤知情的照护方式，你应该怎么做？

options.en: Ask her directly, in front of her partner, whether someone at home is hurting her, so that nothing stays hidden
options.zh: 当着伴侣的面直接问她家里是否有人伤害她，把事情摆到台面上说清楚

options.en: Find a chance to talk with her alone, ask without judgment, offer resources, and share concerns at handover
options.zh: 找机会单独与她交谈，不带评判地询问，提供资源，交接时转达担忧

options.en: Tell her firmly that she must come to hospital, where she will be properly assessed and kept safe
options.zh: 坚决告诉她必须去医院，在那里她才能得到妥善评估和保护

options.en: Tell the partner you suspect abuse and that police will be called, so she knows she is protected
options.zh: 告诉她伴侣你怀疑有虐待、并会报警，让她知道自己受到保护

questions.explanationEn: Victims of intimate partner violence are often evasive and may protect the abuser. A trauma-informed approach centres safety, trust, and control: find an ordinary clinical reason to speak with her alone (for example, in the ambulance), be non-judgmental and supportive, give her as much control as possible, encourage her to think about where she could go or whom she could call, and pass your concerns on at handover. If she declines transport, ask whether it is safe to leave information about services. A is wrong because asking in front of the partner can trigger retaliation, and she is unlikely to answer honestly. C is wrong because ordering a capable adult to hospital removes her control. D is wrong because confronting a possible abuser escalates danger to her and to your crew; scene safety comes first, and police are involved through safe channels.
questions.explanationZh: 亲密伴侣暴力的受害者常常含糊其辞，甚至会维护施暴者。创伤知情的做法以安全、信任和掌控感为核心：借一个寻常的临床理由与她单独交谈（比如在救护车里），不评判、多支持，尽量让她掌握主动，鼓励她想想可以去哪里、可以找谁求助，并在交接时转达你的担忧。如果她拒绝转运，问问留下相关服务的资料是否安全。A 错：当着伴侣的面问，可能招致报复，她也不太可能如实回答。C 错：命令一位有决定能力的成年人去医院，剥夺了她的掌控感。D 错：当面质问可能的施暴者，会让她和班组都陷入更大的危险；现场安全永远第一，报警应通过安全的方式进行。

questions.questionEn: A patient with possible cardiac chest pain speaks little English. You need her consent for a 12-lead ECG and ASA. Her teenage son is present and offers to interpret. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一位疑似心源性胸痛的患者英语能力有限。你需要征得她同意，为她做 12 导联心电图并给予阿司匹林（ASA）。她十几岁的儿子在场，主动提出帮忙翻译。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Accept the son's help for the whole conversation, since she trusts him and he knows her history
options.zh: 整个沟通都请儿子翻译，因为她信任儿子，而且儿子也了解她的病史

options.en: Use simple English with gestures and demonstration, and go ahead once she nods in agreement
options.zh: 用简单英语配合手势和示范，她一点头就开始操作

options.en: Use a professional phone interpreter for the consent talk, relying on the son only for urgent basics
options.zh: 用专业电话翻译完成同意沟通，接通前只借助儿子传达紧急信息

options.en: Hold off on the ECG and ASA until she reaches hospital, where in-person interpreters are readily available
options.zh: 心电图和阿司匹林都等她到了医院、有现场翻译时再做

questions.explanationEn: The first resource for a language barrier is an interpreter, and many EMS services have telephone interpretation for exactly this. A child is a poor interpreter for consent — someone older and less emotionally involved is better — so use the son only for urgent basics until the interpreter is connected. This gives her the same quality of informed consent a fluent English speaker would get. A is wrong because a teenager may soften or leave out information and carries an unfair burden in his mother's emergency. B is wrong because a nod after a few words of English is not informed consent; your gestures are no substitute for an interpreter. D is wrong because the ECG and ASA are time-sensitive for possible cardiac chest pain, and delaying care because of language is itself an inequitable outcome.
questions.explanationZh: 遇到语言障碍，首先要找的是翻译，很多 EMS 机构都有电话翻译服务，正是为这种情况准备的。孩子并不适合为知情同意做翻译——年纪大一些、情感牵连少一些的人更好——所以在接通翻译之前，只借助儿子传达紧急的基本信息。这样她才能得到和英语流利者同样质量的知情同意。A 错：十几岁的孩子可能会弱化或漏掉信息，在母亲的急症中让他承担这个角色也不公平。B 错：说几句英语后对方点头并不等于知情同意，手势比划代替不了翻译。D 错：对疑似心源性胸痛来说，心电图和阿司匹林（ASA）都有时间要求，因为语言问题推迟处置本身就是一种不公平。

questions.questionEn: You are the first unit to arrive at a highway bus rollover. Multiple people are out of the bus, several are still inside, and traffic is still moving past. Fire and police are minutes away. What should you do first?
questions.questionZh: 你是第一个到达高速公路大巴侧翻现场的单元。多人已从车内出来，还有几人被困车内，车流仍在旁边通行。消防和警方还有几分钟才到。你首先应该做什么？

options.en: Begin treating the most seriously injured patient you can reach, since every minute counts
options.zh: 立即救治你能接触到的伤势最重的伤员，因为在这种现场每一分钟都很关键

options.en: Enter the bus to find out exactly how many people are trapped before you call anything in
options.zh: 先进入车内弄清到底有多少人被困，再呼叫任何支援

options.en: Wait for fire and police to arrive before setting up any kind of command structure on scene
options.zh: 等消防和警方到场后再建立任何形式的现场指挥

options.en: Assume command: give a radio size-up, request resources, identify hazards, and begin triage
options.zh: 承担指挥：无线电通报现场概况，请求资源，识别危险，开始检伤分类

questions.explanationEn: The first unit at a multiple-casualty incident sizes up the scene — what do I have, what do I need to do, what resources do I need — reports it, and assumes command until relieved. Safety, early resource requests, and triage do the greatest good; individual treatment waits. A is wrong because committing to one patient leaves the others uncounted and the scene with no commander. B is wrong because entering an unstable bus with traffic still moving puts you at risk and delays the resource request. C is wrong because command should be established early by the first arriving responder, and waiting wastes the minutes when it matters most.
questions.explanationZh: 多人伤亡事件中，第一个到场的单元要先评估现场——有什么情况、需要做什么、需要哪些资源——通报出去，并承担指挥直到被接替。保障安全、尽早请求资源、开始检伤分类，才能发挥最大效益；个体救治要往后放。A 错：投入救治某一个人，其他伤员就没人清点，现场也没有了指挥。B 错：车流还在通行时进入尚未稳定的车厢，会让自己陷入危险，还延误了资源请求。C 错：指挥应由首个到场的人员尽早建立，干等只会浪费最关键的那几分钟。

questions.questionEn: At a house fire you are told two occupants are unaccounted for and one rescued person is in respiratory distress. You have one ambulance on scene. When should you request additional resources?
questions.questionZh: 在一处住宅火灾现场，你被告知有两名住户下落不明，一名已获救者出现呼吸窘迫。现场只有你们一辆救护车。你应该在什么时候请求增援？

options.en: Immediately, based on the possible number of patients, since units can be cancelled later
options.zh: 立即请求，依据是可能的伤员人数——用不上可以之后再取消

options.en: Once the missing occupants have been located and their condition has been confirmed
options.zh: 等找到下落不明的住户、确认他们的伤情之后

options.en: After you have completed a full assessment of the patient already in front of you
options.zh: 在完成对眼前这位患者的全面评估之后

options.en: When the fire department's incident commander tells you that more units are needed
options.zh: 等消防的现场指挥官明确告诉你需要再多调几辆救护车的时候

questions.explanationEn: Deciding what resources you need is part of the initial scene size-up. Resources take time to arrive, so the request is based on the potential patient load, not the confirmed one: over-requesting costs a cancellation, under-requesting costs a patient waiting with no ambulance. B is wrong because by the time the missing occupants are found and assessed, the extra units are still many minutes away. C is wrong because finishing one patient's assessment first delays a request that should go out on arrival. D is wrong because recognizing the need for medical resources is your job; waiting for another agency to prompt you only adds delay.
questions.explanationZh: 判断需要哪些资源，本来就是初步现场评估的一部分。资源到场需要时间，所以请求要基于可能的伤员规模，而不是已确认的人数：多请求的代价只是取消一次，请求不足的代价则是有患者等不到救护车。B 错：等找到并评估完失踪住户，增援车辆还要很多分钟才能到。C 错：先评估完一位患者再请求，会延误本该一到场就发出的请求。D 错：识别医疗资源需求是你的职责，等别的部门提醒只会增加延误。

questions.questionEn: You are running a multi-casualty scene. Two additional PCP crews and four first responders have just arrived and are looking to you. What is the most effective way to deploy them?
questions.questionZh: 你正在指挥一个多人伤亡现场。刚到的两组 PCP 和四名先遣急救员正望向你等待指示。最有效的部署方式是什么？

options.en: Send them to the most seriously injured patients and let them organize the work among themselves
options.zh: 派他们去处理伤势最重的那几名伤员，到了那里再让他们自己商量着分工

options.en: Send each crew to a different part of the scene to search for and treat patients on their own
options.zh: 把每组派到现场不同区域，各自寻找并处理伤员

options.en: Ask each arriving crew which task they would prefer, so people work where they feel strongest
options.zh: 问每个到场班组想承担什么任务，让大家做自己最擅长的事

options.en: Give each crew a specific task by name, state who reports to whom, and confirm each is understood
options.zh: 按车组点名分派具体任务，说明谁向谁汇报，并确认每组都已理解

questions.explanationEn: Assigning responsibilities means explicit, confirmed tasks with a clear reporting structure; the incident command system exists to prevent duplicated effort and freelancing, where units make independent, often inefficient decisions. A is wrong because letting crews organize themselves is freelancing and duplicates effort on the same patients. B is wrong because independent searching leaves no one with a coherent picture of who is where. C is wrong because preference-based assignment can leave critical roles, such as transport coordination, unfilled.
questions.explanationZh: 分派职责意味着明确的、经过确认的任务分配和清晰的汇报关系；事故指挥系统（ICS）的存在，就是为了防止重复劳动和各自为战（freelancing），即各单元各自作出往往低效的决定。A 错：让各组自行分工就是各自为战，会在同几名伤员身上重复用力。B 错：各自搜寻会让谁也掌握不了“谁在哪里”的完整图景。C 错：按个人意愿分工，可能让转运协调等关键角色无人承担。

questions.questionEn: You are treating a patient in an apartment when you notice the man who called 911 has moved between you and the only door, his voice is rising, and he keeps putting his hand in his jacket pocket. What is the priority action?
questions.questionZh: 你正在一间公寓内处置患者，此时注意到打 911 的那名男子已挪到你与唯一出口之间，说话声调不断升高，并反复把手伸进夹克口袋。首要行动是什么？

options.en: Keep treating the patient while your partner talks with the man and tries to calm him down and distract him
options.zh: 继续救治患者，由搭档和该男子交谈，设法让他平静下来、分散他的注意力

options.en: Ask the man directly what he has in his pocket, so you know whether there is a real threat
options.zh: 直接问他口袋里是什么，弄清是否真的有威胁

options.en: Speed up your treatment so you can package the patient and leave as quickly as possible
options.zh: 加快处置速度，尽快打包患者撤离

options.en: Signal your partner, move toward the exit, call police, and leave — with the patient only if safe
options.zh: 暗号提醒搭档，向出口移动，呼叫警察并撤离——安全时才带上患者

questions.explanationEn: Situational awareness means acting the moment the risk picture changes. Never let someone come between you and your exit; call for law enforcement, and leave immediately if you or your partner are in danger — taking the patient only if that can be done safely. A is wrong because it splits the crew while you remain cut off from the only door. B is wrong because challenging him about the pocket can trigger the very assault you fear. C is wrong because packaging takes minutes, during which you remain trapped while the situation escalates.
questions.explanationZh: 情境意识，意味着风险一变化就立即行动。绝不能让对方挡在你和出口之间；要呼叫执法人员，一旦你或搭档有危险就立即撤离——只有能安全做到时才带上患者。A 错：这会让班组分散，而你仍然被堵在唯一的出口之内。B 错：当面质问口袋里是什么，可能正好引发你担心的袭击。C 错：打包患者需要好几分钟，这段时间你一直被困，而局势还在升级。

questions.questionEn: A newly licensed paramedic joins your station. She is visibly nervous and hesitant to ask questions. What best supports her integration?
questions.questionZh: 一位刚取得执照的救护员加入你所在的站点。她明显紧张，也不太敢提问。什么做法最有助于她融入？

options.en: Give her space to find her feet on her own, without drawing extra attention to her nerves
options.zh: 给她空间自己适应，不要特别关注她的紧张

options.en: Assign her only straightforward calls until her confidence improves, to protect both her and her patients
options.zh: 在她建立信心之前只给她安排简单的任务，保护她也保护患者

options.en: Reassure her that everyone struggles at first, and that it gets easier with time and experience
options.zh: 安慰她说人人刚开始都很难，时间和经验多了就好了

options.en: Introduce her around, say plainly that questions are welcome, debrief calls with her, and check in
options.zh: 带她认识大家，明确告诉她欢迎提问，和她一起复盘任务，并定期关心她

questions.explanationEn: Facilitating the integration of new paramedics means acting rather than waiting: explicitly making questions normal dismantles the fear of looking incompetent that keeps new staff silent — and that silence is a patient-safety risk. A is wrong because leaving her alone leaves her questions unasked and her isolated. B is wrong because sheltering her from complexity does nothing about her reluctance to ask, and she will meet complex calls anyway. C is wrong because generic reassurance gives her neither concrete permission to ask nor anyone to ask.
questions.explanationZh: 促进新救护员融入，意味着主动作为而不是等待：明确地把“提问”变成正常的事，才能消除新人怕显得不称职、于是闭口不问的顾虑——而这种沉默本身就是患者安全隐患。A 错：放任她自己摸索，问题没人问，她也一直孤立。B 错：把她和复杂任务隔开，解决不了她不敢提问的问题，复杂任务迟早还是会遇到。C 错：泛泛的安慰既没有明确允许她提问，也没给她一个可以请教的人。

questions.questionEn: Morale at your station has dropped after months of overtime and offload delays. Colleagues are increasingly cynical about doing anything beyond the minimum. You hold no formal leadership position. What can you most usefully do?
questions.questionZh: 在数月的加班和交接延误之后，站里的士气明显下滑。同事们对做任何超出最低要求的事都越来越消极。你并没有任何正式管理职务。你最有用的做法是什么？

options.en: Focus on your own standards and stay out of the negativity, so it doesn't drag you down too
options.zh: 守好自己的标准，远离负面情绪，免得自己也被拖下水

options.en: Wait for management to deal with morale, since the causes are organizational, not personal
options.zh: 等管理层来解决士气问题，毕竟根源在组织而不在个人

options.en: Lead informally: model good practice, recognize good work specifically, and turn complaints into asks
options.zh: 做非正式的带动者：以身作则，具体肯定同事的表现，把抱怨变成诉求

options.en: Organize your colleagues to file a formal group grievance about the workload with management and the union
options.zh: 组织站里的同事们就工作负荷问题，向管理层和工会正式提出集体申诉

questions.explanationEn: Motivating colleagues to strive for excellence is situational leadership — it does not need a title. Visible standards, specific recognition of good work, and turning diffuse frustration into concrete requests leadership can act on are what shift a demoralized culture. A is wrong because withdrawing into your own practice concedes the culture to cynicism. B is wrong because it ignores the influence you already have with your peers. D is wrong because a grievance may be a legitimate route for workload concerns, but it does nothing about the cynicism eroding standards at the station, which is what the question asks you to address.
questions.explanationZh: 激励同事追求卓越属于情境式领导——不需要头衔。看得见的执业标准、具体地肯定同事的好表现，把弥散的不满整理成管理层可以着手的具体诉求，才能扭转低落的风气。A 错：退回到自己的一亩三分地，等于把站里的风气让给了犬儒心态。B 错：这忽视了你在同事中本来就有的影响力。D 错：集体申诉也许是反映工作负荷的正当途径，但对正在侵蚀站里执业标准的犬儒风气毫无作用，而这才是题目要你应对的问题。

questions.questionEn: Which feature best characterizes a workplace culture that genuinely promotes patient safety?
questions.questionZh: 哪项特征最能体现一个真正促进患者安全的职场文化？

options.en: Errors are investigated thoroughly, and the individuals responsible are identified, disciplined, and retrained
options.zh: 错误都会被彻查，找出责任人，给予处分并安排再培训

options.en: Incident reports are rare, because staff follow protocols closely and few errors are recorded
options.zh: 不良事件报告很少，因为员工都严格遵守规程，几乎没有什么错误被记录下来

options.en: Experienced staff take the high-risk calls, so that errors are less likely to happen at all
options.zh: 由资深员工承担高风险任务，从根本上减少出错

options.en: Staff report errors and near misses without fear, and findings drive system fixes shared with crews
options.zh: 员工可以无惧追责地报告错误和险情，结论会推动系统改进并反馈给一线

questions.explanationEn: A genuine patient-safety culture depends on reporting without fear, analysis that looks for system causes, and visible feedback that closes the loop; without these, hazards stay hidden. A is wrong because focusing on the individual drives reporting underground, and most errors have system contributors that retraining one person will not fix. B is wrong because a low reporting rate usually signals under-reporting, not safety. C is wrong because shielding less experienced staff from risk prevents them from learning and leaves the underlying system unchanged.
questions.explanationZh: 真正的患者安全文化依赖三点：无惧追责的上报、着眼于系统原因的分析，以及看得见的反馈闭环；缺了这些，隐患就始终藏在暗处。A 错：盯着个人追责会把上报逼入地下，而且大多数错误都有系统层面的诱因，培训某一个人解决不了。B 错：上报率低通常意味着瞒报漏报，而不是安全。C 错：把经验较浅的员工与风险隔开，既让他们学不到东西，背后的系统问题也原封不动。

questions.questionEn: Several crews at your station have mentioned that a critical airway item is stored in a different compartment on the newer ambulances than on the older ones. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 站里好几个班组都提到，一件关键气道器材在新款救护车上的存放位置和旧款不一样。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Remind crews to check where everything is during the vehicle check at the start of each and every shift
options.zh: 提醒各班组在每个班次开始做车辆检查时，都逐一确认每样东西放在哪里

options.en: Label the compartment on your own truck with tape, and suggest others do the same on theirs
options.zh: 自己用胶带给车上那个隔舱贴上标签，并建议其他人也照做

options.en: Report it through your service's safety or quality system as a hazard, and suggest standardizing it
options.zh: 通过机构的安全或质量报告系统把它作为隐患上报，并建议统一存放位置

options.en: Mention it informally to someone from fleet services the next time you happen to see them
options.zh: 下次碰到车队部门的人时随口提一下

questions.explanationEn: Inconsistent equipment locations across a fleet are a hidden system hazard: under stress, crews reach for where the item “should” be, and seconds are lost in an airway emergency. Identifying this as a practice-improvement opportunity and reporting it through the formal system puts it in front of the people who can standardize the fleet. A is wrong because it relies on memory under stress and leaves the hazard in place, especially when crews move between trucks. B is wrong because a home-made label on one truck does not fix the fleet and may conflict with equipment standards. D is wrong because an informal mention leaves no record, no owner, and no follow-up.
questions.explanationZh: 同一车队里器材存放位置不统一，是一种隐蔽的系统隐患：压力之下，人会伸手去“应该在”的地方拿，气道急症时就会白白耽误几秒钟。把它看作实践改进的机会，通过正式系统上报，才能让有权统一全车队标准的人知道。A 错：这依赖高压下的记忆，隐患本身并没有消除，班组在不同车辆之间轮换时尤其如此。B 错：在一辆车上自制标签解决不了整个车队的问题，还可能与装备标准相冲突。D 错：私下随口一提，没有记录、没有负责人，也没有后续跟进。

questions.questionEn: Your service launches a quality improvement project on stroke recognition and asks crews to complete a short screening tool on every suspected stroke call. Some colleagues call it "more paperwork." What is the most professional stance?
questions.questionZh: 你所属机构启动了一项卒中识别的质量改进项目，要求各班组在每次疑似卒中任务中填写一份简短的筛查工具表。有些同事称之为"又多了文书活"。最专业的立场是什么？

options.en: Complete the tool only on calls where a stroke diagnosis seems likely, to save time on others
options.zh: 只在卒中诊断比较明确的任务里填写，其余的省点时间

options.en: Complete it as required, but agree with colleagues that its clinical value is probably limited
options.zh: 按要求填写，但附和同事们的看法，认为这份工具的临床价值大概相当有限

options.en: Wait to see whether the project produces useful findings before taking part fully yourself
options.zh: 先看看项目能否得出有用结论，再决定是否全面参与

options.en: Use it on every suspected stroke, ask what it measures, and give feedback if it proves impractical
options.zh: 每次疑似卒中都填写，了解它要测量什么，如在现场确实不实用就提出反馈

questions.explanationEn: Supporting improvement initiatives means engaging constructively: consistent data collection is what makes the findings valid, understanding the purpose sustains participation, and constructive feedback improves the tool. A is wrong because selective completion biases the data — the project needs every suspected stroke, including those that turn out not to be strokes. B is wrong because complying while openly doubting it erodes everyone else's participation. C is wrong because the findings depend on participation now; waiting for results guarantees there will be none.
questions.explanationZh: 支持工作中的改进项目，意味着建设性地参与：数据收集一致，结论才能成立；理解项目目的，参与才能持续；建设性反馈则能改进工具本身。A 错：选择性填写会让数据产生偏倚——项目需要的是所有疑似卒中病例，包括最后证实不是卒中的。B 错：表面照做、嘴上唱衰，会削弱其他人的参与。C 错：结论要靠现在的参与才能得出，等有了结果再参与，就注定不会有结果。

questions.questionEn: You have been running command at a multi-casualty scene for 12 minutes with triage underway. A supervisor arrives and says she is assuming command. What is the correct process?
questions.questionZh: 你已在一个多人伤亡现场担任指挥 12 分钟，检伤分类正在进行中。一位主管到场，表示要接管指挥。正确的流程是什么？

options.en: Hand her your triage tags and notes, and return to patient care immediately without delay
options.zh: 把检伤标签和笔记交给她，马上回去救治伤员

options.en: Keep command until the incident is over, since changing command partway causes confusion
options.zh: 保留指挥权直到事件结束，因为中途换指挥会造成混乱

options.en: Keep running triage while she handles the resource requests, without any formal transfer of command
options.zh: 不做正式移交，你继续负责检伤分类，资源请求那一块就交给她来负责

options.en: Brief her face to face on patients, resources, assignments, and hazards, then announce the change
options.zh: 当面简报伤员、资源、分工和危险，确认后用无线电通报指挥权变更

questions.explanationEn: An incident commander may hand command to someone more experienced, but the transfer must be orderly and, if possible, face to face, following your service's procedures: patient count and triage status, resources requested and en route, who is doing what, hazards, and what remains — then explicit confirmation and an announcement so everyone knows who is in charge. A is wrong because handing over tags without a briefing loses the whole situational picture. B is wrong because it blocks an appropriate escalation to a more experienced commander. C is wrong because split or unclear command is one of the most dangerous failure modes at a multiple-casualty incident.
questions.explanationZh: 现场指挥可以把指挥权交给更有经验的人，但移交必须有序，尽量面对面，并按机构的程序进行：伤员人数与检伤进度、已申请和在途的资源、谁在做什么、现场危险，以及还有哪些待办——随后明确确认，并通报给所有人，让大家都知道谁在负责。A 错：不做简报只交标签，会丢失全部现场情况。B 错：这阻碍了把指挥权合理地交给更有经验的指挥者。C 错：指挥权分裂或不清，是多人伤亡事件中最危险的失效方式之一。
